data.title: French student protests: 'There's been lack of investment in education for years now'
data.description: Eve Irvine is pleased to welcome Axel Berra-Vescio, French History-Geography and European section teacher in the Paris region. France's student protests are exposing what educators describe as years of structural neglect, widening educational inequalities and the cumulative consequences of controversial reforms. “We've been ignored basically about every demand we made,” Berra-Vescio says. He also condemns the police response to the demonstrations, warning that repression is unlikely to weaken a movement rooted in years of frustration over the future of public education.

data.title: 'Quite horrifying': Afghan economic crisis leaves EU deportees with 'very little' to return to
data.description: Europe's increasingly pragmatic engagement with Afghanistan's Taliban rulers is exposing a fundamental contradiction between diplomatic non-recognition and political necessity. In an investigation for The New York Times, Pakistan and Afghanistan bureau chief Elian Peltier reveals how European governments are quietly expanding negotiations with the Taliban over migrant deportations, diplomatic representation and economic assistance. “Even though on paper European governments do not recognise the Taliban administration, in practice they meet much more frequently than most of us know,” Peltier explains.

data.title: ‘Not a problem of short-term solutions’: French students demand structural change, better conditions
data.description: Delano D'Souza is pleased to welcome Gökçe Tuncel, Sociologist and post-doctoral researcher associated with the Université Paris-Est Créteil (UPEC) and the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences (EHESS) in Paris. What began as a protest over missing teachers and inadequate resources at a high school in Créteil has rapidly evolved into a wider mobilization challenging structural inequalities within France’s public education system. “This is not a problem of short-term solutions. This is a structural problem that they are denouncing, and their demands are structural changes,” explains Tuncel. The movement's rapid expansion reflects a growing political consciousness among young people confronting deteriorating educational infrastructure, unequal access to resources, and an increasingly uncertain future.

data.title: ISS mission: 'It's really exciting to see this renewal of French women in space'
data.description: More than six decades after thirteen pioneering women demonstrated they could meet the same demanding physical tests as America's first male astronauts, gender equality in space exploration remains an unfinished journey, explains Laurène Delsupexhe, Chemical Propulsion Engineer at the European Space Agency. From the institutional exclusion of the Mercury 13 to the renewed ambitions of NASA's Artemis programme, Delsupexhe traces the remarkable progress of women in space while exposing the persistent barriers that have outlasted generations of scientific and technological breakthroughs. With astronaut recruitment approaching gender parity, she argues that the next frontier is not simply reaching the Moon, but ensuring that women are fully represented in shaping humanity's future beyond Earth.

data.title: The housing crisis is now global. It shows just how undemocratic our nations have become  | Leilani Farha
data.description: When we can’t even afford to rent or buy somewhere to live, we have to ask: did we give the financial sector too much power? Leilani Farha is the former UN special rapporteur on adequate housing In the summer of 2021, I visited a homeless community in a park in Toronto, Canada, and spoke to one of the residents. He was living in a tent in the shadow of brand new skyscrapers, and had been homeless for about five years. At one point he swivelled around, pointed up at a crane on the skyline, and said: “Who are they building those for? Definitely not for me.” He was right. And he captured something experienced by ordinary people around the world: the growing conviction that the housing system is no longer tethered to their needs. What he was pointing at is not just a housing crisis. It is a crisis of democracy. Leilani Farha is the 2026 CBC Massey lecturer. This piece is based on her new book: Housing Inc.: A Global Takeover and Our Fight for Home . She is the former UN special rapporteur on adequate housing and the global director of the international human rights organisation, The Shift Continue reading...

data.title: Tony Hall has lived in the UK for 50 years. Why is the Home Office trying to deport him?
data.description: He arrived in the UK aged 12, but for the last 14 years Hall has been under threat of being sent back to Barbados – a country he doesn’t remember and where he has no surviving relatives When Tony Hall was released from detention in 2012, his family rallied around to support him. One of his five older sisters said he could stay with her for a while. A nephew printed business cards and designed a website for him so he could advertise his services as a painter and decorator, to make the most of the vocational training he received while he served his prison sentence. But for 14 years he has been unable to make use of the cards because of a Home Office decision that he should be deported. All this time he has been kept on a deportation list, which means he cannot work, rent somewhere to live, receive benefits or do anything that would allow him to start rebuilding his life. Instead, he remains on the edge of destitution, reliant on the kindness of family and friends to survive. Continue reading...

data.title: Tap water no longer drinkable in Norwegian town as climate-related thawing releases heavy metals
data.description: Warning for other Arctic communities as residents told not to use water in Longyearbyen in Svalbard, one of the fastest-warming places in the world Residents of a remote town in Norway that is in one of the fastest-warming places in the world have been told they must no longer drink tap water due to heavy metal contamination that scientists have linked to the thawing permafrost. Longyearbyen, in the archipelago of Svalbard , gets its main drinking water supply from a 1.5 mile-long (2.5km) dammed lake called Isdammen, or “ice pond”. Higher temperatures as a result of the climate crisis have thawed permafrost, leading to newly exposed bedrock leaching metals into the pond. Continue reading...

data.title: The one change that worked: I deleted Instagram – and embraced the joys of a truly private life
data.description: I’d become obsessed with appealing to my invisible audience. But since I ditched the app a year ago, my quieter moments have taken on brilliant new meaning I first downloaded Instagram when I was 17 and became hooked on it the way most people fall in love: slowly, and then all at once. For a long time, I never considered myself a social media addict. I self-righteously refused to download TikTok, declared Snapchat to be for “children”, and posted less regularly on Instagram than half of the people I followed. As I went through my university years, however, certain changes crept up on me. I began to swap reading – or essay-writing – for hours spent curating new posts. On my way home from lectures (or later, from my work as a journalist), I would spend ages trying to take the artsiest, most perfect picture of that evening’s sunset for my story – as if the people who followed me were eagerly awaiting yet another photo of one of the Earth’s rotations. What usually followed was a night of reloading my feed to see how many people had reacted to my post – or worse, hadn’t reacted at all. Continue reading...

data.title: Michael Kiwanuka: Fudge review – rough and instinctive, but also lush and alive with melody
data.description: (Polydor) Its release delayed by ill health, Kiwanuka’s latest was made in tandem with 2024’s Small Changes – but it’s much more than a mere companion album In November 2024, Michael Kiwanuka released his fourth album, Small Changes , an extremely poised and self-assured piece of work. After three gold albums, a Grammy nomination, a Mercury prize win and the ongoing success of Cold Little Heart , a 2017 single hoisted to virality and million-selling status in the US after its use in TV drama Big Little Lies, Kiwanuka – and his long-term production collaborators Danger Mouse and Inflo – evidently felt confident enough to release a beautiful but wilfully understated album. Recorded in LA, some impressive names lurked in the credits: legendary session musicians including bassist Pino Palladino and the drummer James Gadson, who played on Marvin Gaye’s I Want You and Donald Fagen’s The Nightfly; the similarly legendary R&B producer Jimmy Jam served as organist on three tracks. It attracted the kind of critical praise in which adjectives like “unhurried” and “meditative” figured heavily. But it also wasn’t the whole story. It turned out there was a second album, its songs written – or rather, jammed into existence by Kiwanuka and members of his live band – concurrently with Small Changes. It was made not in LA but in a studio that “looks like a medieval hut” in Southampton. August session musicians and legendary R&B producers were not present during its recording, nor were Danger Mouse and Inflo. Indeed, you could read its opening track, Summer Clothes , as a kind of Dear John letter to both of them (“I’m OK, I found another way … we’ll be back here soon, just not today”). Continue reading...

data.title: Is it true that … you need to take 10,000 steps a day to be healthy?
data.description: The fitness benchmark has surprisingly unscientific origins – yet it does contain more than a kernel of truth The idea that we need to walk 10,000 steps a day originated not in medical research but in a 1960s marketing campaign for a pedometer, says Jack McNamara, senior lecturer in clinical exercise physiology at the University of East London. The round number was easy to remember and the idea caught on, despite there being no scientific evidence for 10,000 steps as a specific threshold for health. “When the research community looked into it, they found that there were health benefits, so it didn’t necessarily get thrown out as pseudoscience,” says McNamara. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘When they listen to this song, they know food is coming’: Burrolandia, a donkey obsession
data.description: Twenty years ago, Germán Flores founded a refuge for donkeys that faced abandonment, exploitation or slaughter, in memory of Roberto, a working donkey from his childhood. Once synonymous with the country, Mexico’s donkey population has plummeted in recent years. Burrolandia was founded in response to these dwindling numbers to provide dignified living conditions to about 100 ‘burritos’ who have suffered exploitation and abuse around Mexico Twenty years ago, Germán Flores decided to start preserving the Mexican donkey, an endangered species with about 300,000 remaining in the whole country. Flores was inspired to take care of donkeys after learning that the donkey population in Mexico had decreased by about 60% between 1994 and 2010. It was a natural decision for him: the donkeys are part of the identity of his town, Otumba in Mexico State. But while the annual national donkey fair purports to celebrate the animal, around the country they are also routinely mistreated. Flores carries a young donkey at his sanctuary Continue reading...

data.title: The problem with telling people the world is ending
data.description: In the face of terrible crises, it can feel right to shock people into action. But what if that has the opposite effect? These days, it’s easy to succumb to hopelessness. Whether you’re thinking about the climate crisis, the prospect of AI apocalypse, war or political turmoil, the list of challenges facing humanity can seem insurmountable. It certainly feels unprecedented, and much of it may be. The sense of impending doom, on the other hand, is nothing new. And what we have learned from the past is that doomerism can lead to paralysis. If everyone freezes, then nothing changes – but if we want to have a chance of mitigating some of the threats I’ve mentioned then action is what’s required. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘A vigorous apologist for a cruel emperor’: Is Caryl Churchill’s explosive new play about Trump and his press officers?
data.description: From Thatcherism to global crisis to an ever-online world, she has chronicled our race to the abyss. Now she’s written a play about a blond-wigged voicepiece for an un-named, strongman ruler. Who can she mean? Triumph, which has just opened at London’s Almeida theatre, is Caryl Churchill’s latest piece of explosive minimalism. Running at just 20 minutes, it skewers contemporary barbarism without mentioning the names of Trump, Putin or any of the other supposedly strong national leaders. It works through historical analogy and is a reminder that Churchill – while “always ahead of the game” in the words of the play’s director, James Macdonald – has in recent years developed a form of elliptical drama for which the apt word might be compressionism. At the heart of Churchill’s new play is an edgy romance between a male journalist and a female press officer who dons a blond wig for her screen appearances and who is a vigorous apologist for a cruel, vindictive, narcissistic emperor. Continue reading...

data.title: I saw rioting, looting, above all, anger. If French leaders think more violence will solve this, they’re mistaken | Oliver Haynes
data.description: It’s a perfect storm of protesters with heartfelt grievances and others set on conflict. The key here is the sense of betrayal that united them on the streets The first thing I learned on the streets of Paris this weekend is that there is no arguing with teargas. I arrived at Place de la République just after 1pm yesterday. The mood was festive until police started firing volleys of teargas into the square from Rue du Faubourg-du-Temple. I didn’t see the inciting incident – if there even was one – and tried walking into the cloud of CS gas hanging in the air. It was impossible. The gas clings to your nose and burns your eyes, and you quickly start struggling to breathe. I retreated towards the Boulevard de Magenta, blinking furiously to stop the stinging. Oliver Haynes is a journalist and co-host of Sacré Bleu: the French presidential election podcast Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? data.title: This carnival of protest on the streets of Delhi has shaken Narendra Modi like nothing before | Meena Kandasamy
data.description: The singing, dancing and sheer joy in the face of police brutality at the protests led by the Cockroach Janta party show people no longer fear India’s regime In July, as supporters of the Cockroach movement took to Jantar Mantar , the designated protest site in Delhi, incensed over exam-paper leaks and demanding the resignation of India’s education minister, the rest of the nation realised that for the first time since the Bharatiya Janata party (BJP) came to power in 2014, the curse of inertia and the grip of fear had been smashed irrevocably. Prime minister Narendra Modi’s image of invincibility has been punctured. People in India have been conditioned to believe in an idea of intense slow-burn protests that eventually bring change – but the Cockroaches have shown us that the revolution can be fast-tracked. Meena Kandasamy is a poet and writer based in Chennai Continue reading...

data.title: The Guardian view on plague in Russia: what is most worrying is the lack of information | Editorial
data.description: In the three weeks since a health worker’s death in Siberia, officials have stonewalled the WHO – setting a worrying precedent for future pandemics Is there a plague outbreak in Russia? If the answer were a clear yes, there shouldn’t be much reason to worry. With swift medical intervention, plague is treatable. But in the nearly three weeks since a worker at a Siberian plague research unit died of a mysterious respiratory illness, state officials have been consistently tight-lipped about what happened and whether there were any further cases. It is this uncertainty that has the World Health Organization (WHO) and international community worried: partly because there is a – very small – risk of an outbreak, and partly because it is yet another warning that the international coordination we rely on to prevent pandemics is fraying along with the rest of international politics, and could easily fail to protect us in the future. Continue reading...

Here we have the man who hired the man. The man who fires the man. The man who also hired or rehired the previous two men he had to fire. Berrada was poached from Manchester City on the basis of his ability to grow commercial revenue (yes, OK, stop laughing), and appears, like everyone else with any actual reach around here, to exist in a strangely consequence-free bubble. data.title: Northampton break England’s duck in Champions Cup with victory over Cardiff
data.description: Pool 4: Northampton 28-12 Cardiff Saints claim first win for Prem side at eighth time of asking At 7.16pm, just around the time those Sunday night blues kick in, England’s Champions Cup cohort finally had something to cheer about. It was not pretty but after seven of their Prem rivals had failed to claim victory in the opening round of the competition, Saints survived a sizeable scare from Cardiff to put one on the board for the Prem, thanks in no small part to the excellent George Hendy. It might be harsh on some of the performances this weekend – Gloucester were immense in drawing with Bordeaux, Exeter mightily unlucky to be beaten in Toulouse – but zero wins would have been a crushing embarrassment for a league that has been feted for its attacking exploits so far this season. One out of eight is not a lot to shout about as it is. Continue reading...

data.title: Another unremarkable win shows Arsenal’s strength is in depth rather than creativity | Jonathan Wilson
data.description: Champions so risk-averse Forest were lured into thinking they had a chance, until bench was used to see them off Pass. Pass. Pass. Pass. Sideways. Square. Backwards. Pass. Pass. Recycle. Pass. It wasn’t much of a spectacle. But in the end, for the second week running, thanks in no small part of their bench, Arsenal won. Fireworks in the autumn are for Bonfire Night; titles require relentless accumulation. Since the international break, Arsenal have won three games out of three despite not being in the lead at half-time in any of them. Hammered at Brighton and having endured a drab first hour at home to Leeds last week, there has been a rare sense, for the first time really since Manchester City dropped points at Everton at the beginning of May, of Arsenal not being quite at their best, needing to reassert their quality. This was not a performance that would terrify any opponent, but it did highlight Arsenal’s consistency and it did demonstrate just how deep their squad now runs. Continue reading...

data.title: Safety concerns mount over Japan’s traditional festivals after string of fatal accidents
data.description: Deputy mayor of Saijo died after becoming trapped under float, days after two similar incidents elsewhere There is mounting concern over the safety of Japan’s traditional festivals after the death of a senior local official who was reportedly crushed beneath a float at the weekend, days after two men died in similar incidents in another part of the country. Akihiro Nabae, the deputy mayor of Saijo, in western Japan, was carrying a giant float with other participants in a festival on Saturday when he became trapped beneath the structure, Agence France-Presse reported. Nabae, 62, was taken to hospital and later pronounced dead, local media said, adding that no one else was injured. Continue reading...

data.title: Elizabeth Holmes documentary You Can See Everything debuts with huge $15m opening weekend
data.description: Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s buzzy film was shown on only 855 screens in the biggest documentary opening in North America since Fahrenheit 9/11 in 2004 Nathan Fielder’s nearly three-hour Elizabeth Holmes documentary, You Can See Everything , has opened to an extraordinary $15m domestic box office, the biggest opening weekend for a documentary in North America in more than 20 years. You Can See Everything, directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, made $15m (A$21.5m, £11.2m) from only 855 screens, and had more than 2,000 sold-out screenings at the weekend, according to the production company A24. It is the biggest opening for a film playing on fewer than 1,000 screens since Borat opened to $26.5m in 2006. Continue reading...

data.title: A California town’s beaches are washing away. Can its residents turn the tide?
data.description: Rapid coastal erosion threatens coastal homes and economies, and as Super El Niño rounds the corner, a town is reckoning with the reality of climate crisis San Clemente is one of southern California’s most picture-perfect beach towns – a capital of American surf culture since the 1950s. In two years, 2028 Olympic surfers will compete at Lower Trestles, a world-class surfing beach. But the town’s longtime cultural and economic driver, its beaches, are now under threat. As pounding waves driven by late-summer storms in the Pacific devour chunks of the California coastline, some of San Clemente’s beaches are growing narrower, the sand increasingly eaten away. data.title: ‘You reach a tipping point’: New Zealand’s strained healthcare system at centre of election battle
data.description: With care shortfalls biting across the country, the National-led coalition has been accused of letting chronic underfunding worsen Back when she was healthy, Jane Harrison worked for the community – securing money for playgrounds, getting kids into sport and making sure her small town in New Zealand’s South Island was ready if an earthquake struck. Now, she and her husband, Shaun Fitzgerald, 65, are both on disability assistance. Last year, when Fitzgerald – a roofer – was waiting for back surgery for spinal stenosis, Harrison left her job to help look after him at home. The operation in August 2025 was not as effective as hoped. He has since been back into the emergency department in intense pain, waiting for hours with severe cramping, she says. “We called the paramedics recently and they said: ‘There’s no beds in hospital, if we take you you’ll have to sit and you clearly can’t, you’re better off at home.’” Continue reading...

data.title: Vatican upholds excommunication of US deacon who resigned after son was molested by priest
data.description: Scott Peyton joined the Anglicans after the crime against his son. Then the Catholic church officially expelled him The Roman Catholic church has upheld the excommunication of a Louisiana deacon who resigned from the clergy after a priest molested his son. Scott Peyton learned of the decision by the Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith (DDF) – the Vatican entity in charge of Catholic clerical discipline – on Friday in a meeting with the bishop of the diocese of Lafayette, J Douglas Deshotel. The DDF cited technical grounds in rejecting Peyton’s appeal, saying he had joined an Anglican congregation, “published [that] fact … on social media” and therefore refused to submit to the Catholic pope, who since May 2025 has been Leo XIV . Continue reading...

data.title: Emperor of Nothing by Blake J Harris review – the definitive portrait of Larry David
data.description: The Seinfeld creator went from luckless standup to multi-millionaire – but what’s his secret? Larry David agreed to this authorised biography with a five-word email: “Oh Jesus. If we must.” As Blake J Harris tells it, the comedy writer has always been adept at finding reasons not to do something, or to stop doing it, even when there’s nothing to fall back on. As a peppery standup in 1970s New York, David was notorious for storming off stage if the audience displeased him. He walked out of his first TV job, on the Saturday Night Live clone Fridays, because “I stunk.” He twice quit Seinfeld, the sitcom he co-created in 1989, over meddling by NBC executives and fantasised about the network giving him an excuse to leave for good. In 1992, just before it became the biggest show in America, he told friends, “Honestly, I would rather spend a year in prison than do another season of Seinfeld. It would be peaceful. Nobody would make me write anything.” He was only half joking. David’s career proves that it is in fact possible to be immensely, groundbreakingly successful without ever displaying great ambition. Growing up in Brooklyn amid a boisterous extended family, Lawrence Gene David loved baseball and tall tales but, oddly, not making people laugh. “I can’t recall him ever saying a funny thing,” remembers his older brother Ken. After a spell in the army reserve, he drifted through low-effort jobs – limo driver, bra salesman – and dropped out of acting school, partly because his classmate Jeff Goldblum showed him what a real actor looked like. “Most of the time I was just waiting for other people to stop talking so that I could start talking,” he admits. Continue reading...

data.title: Ghost in the Cell review – Indonesian prison-slasher-satire contains the most unhinged punch-up in decades
data.description: Director Joko Anwar uses horror for social commentary as he skewers corruption and hypocrisy with likable silliness and raucous energy Given the 2020s horror boom, Indonesia’s prolific Joko Anwar – who has worked more often in that genre than any other – should be better known. Using horror for social commentary, as Anwar has done often in the past, this prison-slasher-satire features the kind of scabrous broadsides against injustice you see in Bong Joon-ho’s films, and Park Chan-wook’s recent No Other Choice . But in skewering the corruption and hypocrisy of the director’s native country, it has its own likable silliness and raucous energy. As the inmates keep saying: this is Indonesia, not Norway! Fitted up for the murder of his boss, who is found gutted and spreadeagled on a ceiling fan, timid investigative journalist Dimas (Endy Arfian) winds up in the slammer. But murder, immediately followed by the flamboyant flaying of the victim, dogs him wherever he goes: the prison hitman assigned to dispose of him is in turn found in the washroom rendered into flesh origami. Charismatic prison refusenik Anggoro (Abimana Aryasatya) takes Dimas under his wing; as the victims stack up, an apparently clairvoyant member of his clique called Six (Yoga Pratama) admits that all of them manifested a red aura, signifying anger, prior to dying. Continue reading...

data.title: After the Snowmelt review – a fatal disaster in a snowstorm leads to devastating act of remembrance
data.description: Yi-Shan Lo returns to Nepal to follow the route of her best friend’s ill-fated hike in a harrowing but cathartic documentary A work of deep personal reckoning, Yi-Shan Lo’s debut documentary feature opens with closeups of the film-maker’s own footsteps as she trudges through a snowbound landscape. Her jagged movement mirrors the rugged trajectory of the film itself, which grapples with a harrowing tragedy. In 2017, Lo was about to join her best friends Chun and Yueh on their hiking trip across Nepal when she came down with a sudden illness; she decided to stay behind while the other two carried on. Disaster struck: the pair went missing during a heavy snowstorm and were not found for more than 40 days. Yueh survived, but Chun died from lack of food coupled with hypothermia. Struggling to make sense of these events, Lo painstakingly retraces the days leading up to and during her friends’ disappearance. She pores over old text messages, Chun’s diaries and footage captured by the Nepali rescue team. These materials shed some light on the ordeal, as well as the pair’s backgrounds. Diving into her personal archive, Lo recalls her burgeoning friendship with Chun at their Catholic girls’ school, where the latter defiantly resisted the institution’s rigid dress codes. Considering Chun’s efforts to express his non-conforming identity and his use of male pronouns, it is even more devastating that he was repeatedly misgendered in death by various news reports. Continue reading...

She pores over old text messages, Chun’s diaries and footage captured by the Nepali rescue team. These materials shed some light on the ordeal, as well as the pair’s backgrounds. Diving into her personal archive, Lo recalls her burgeoning friendship with Chun at their Catholic girls’ school, where the latter defiantly resisted the institution’s rigid dress codes. Considering Chun’s efforts to express his non-conforming identity and his use of male pronouns, it is even more devastating that he was repeatedly misgendered in death by various news reports. However, Dr Rory Loughnane, a leading scholar and co-author of the research, told the Guardian that computerised textual analysis pushed the case “beyond any reasonable doubt” that the Stratford-born playwright was the principal writer. data.title: ‘Medieval romance overflowed with sexually active fairies’: the surprisingly long roots of romantasy
data.description: Critics mock it as raunchy trash – but this enchanting genre is much older, and wilder, than you might imagine There’s a popular genre, filled with beautiful, human-sized fairies having sex with humans (often quite violent sex, but the people reading it seem to enjoy it). Word is that it’s badly written and unashamedly escapist – all golden, glittering palaces, wild adventure and, of course, gorgeous fairies. It’s certainly popular – plenty of the stories have been translated into numerous languages, spreading across continents. Serious commentators are sure it spells bad news: at best, it’s just a load of trash; at worst, it’s actively leading people astray. Most damningly of all, women produce and consume it. Welcome to the 12th century, where fairy romance is all the rage. Sound familiar? The romantasy that fills our shelves and bestseller lists – from Sarah J Maas’s A Court of Thorns and Roses to Callie Hart’s Quicksilver – is not a new genre, but part of a centuries-old heritage. You only need to look at the medieval predecessors of the modern romantasy novel to understand why it’s enjoyed by millions and why, even after hundreds of years, fairy romance has such power over us – and why there are still those who want to diminish and dismiss it. Continue reading...

data.title: Spaghetti with lentils, and aubergine veggie-balls: Jacob Kenedy’s autumn pasta recipes
data.description: A deliciously humble lentil and spaghetti dish, and a meat-free riff on meatball pasta made with aubergine veggie-balls Some plant-based pasta dishes are light, bright and summery – pesto genovese , tomato sauce, aglio e olio – but some have an umami and complexity that is normally associated with more carnal pleasures. Here are two. Pasta with lentils is a firm personal and family favourite – my mum and I make this dish whenever we fancy something really comforting, and the earthiness of the lentils plays against grassy olive oil and parsley, and the texture of the pasta. True cucina povera – a humble meal, and deliciously so. Veggie-balls are also great things. Polpette (normally translated as meatballs) is just balls (of anything pulped), after all. They can be made of white fish, oily fish or vegetables. I particularly love courgette for its bright, green, fresh flavour, and, above all, rich, velvety, chocolatey aubergine. Of course, you can eat them on their own, but I also love them through pasta, as a vegetarian riff on spaghetti and meatballs. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘This is horrifying. This is madness’: the row over competitive yoga
data.description: Some yogis welcome the idea of competition – for others, it is anathema. Will those keen for yoga to become an Olympic sport win the argument? Vaishnavi Saravanakumar describes herself on Instagram as “India’s rubber band girl”. In a typical video post , dressed in a rhinestone-studded crimson catsuit and accompanied by a Bollywood-rap anthem, she demonstrates an improbable feat. From standing, she snakes into a deep back bend, curls her head and shoulders up under her tiger-striped calves, and finishes beaming to camera with ankles crossed under her chin. This is yoga as we have seldom seen it before. Earlier this year, the Indian government announced that it will push for yogasana’s inclusion in the Olympics, ahead of the country’s bid to host the 2036 Games. The news came the week before the inaugural World Yogasana Championship, held in Ahmedabad in June, at which Saravanakumar, a gold medallist, was one of 522 yogis competing. Continue reading...

data.title: How to make the perfect poires belle Hélène – recipe | Felicity Cloake's How to make the perfect …
data.description: Cool, juicy pears, cold ice-cream, hot chocolate sauce and a crunchy garnish – the perfect pudding It’s always slightly embarrassing to realise that you’ve missed a pop culture reference, even if it’s 162 years old, so I won’t dwell on the fact that until last week I was unaware of the existence of Offenbach’s 1864 operetta about Helen of Troy, La Belle Hélène , after which today’s dish is named. In any case, the great French chef Escoffier was so moved by it, or perhaps by its popularity among Parisian diners, to name this simple dessert of vanilla-scented poached pears topped with hot chocolate sauce after the work’s heroine, played by the comely Hortense Schneider. Though other homages (he includes no fewer than five dishes with that name in his 1907 Guide Culinaire , none of which involve pears) may, like the music, have faded from public consciousness, this particular pairing, if you’ll forgive the pun, has stood the test of time. As Nigel Slater observes in Tender: Volume 2, “The marriage of pears and chocolate is extraordinary. It is as if they were made for each other.” This, I think, is the duo at its “most sumptuous”. Continue reading...

data.title: Great Pottery Throw Down judge Keith Brymer Jones looks back: ‘Men like seeing me be emotional’
data.description: The potter and presenter on a tricky childhood, his religious calling for clay, and cross-dressing as Adele Born in London in 1965, Keith Brymer Jones is a potter, ceramic designer and TV judge. After a stint as lead singer of the punk band the Wigs, he became an apprentice at Harefield Pottery in London. He went on to set up his own company, and created pots and homewares for retailers including Conran, Habitat and Laura Ashley, before developing his signature Word range . He has been a judge on The Great Pottery Throw Down since it started in 2015. His new book, Firing Earth: An Unexpected History of Pots and Potters, is published on 22 October. This photo was taken in our family home in Finchley. Socks, shorts and a T-shirt was my usual outfit for scabbing around in the garden aged 11. I was a complete and utter square. Continue reading...

data.title: Warning signs could predict inflammatory bowel disease a decade before diagnosis
data.description: Antibody patterns in the blood may help doctors identify people at risk so they can be treated earlier, research shows Patterns of antibodies in people’s blood could predict the onset of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) a decade before diagnosis, according to research that raises hopes for catching the condition early. Crohn’s disease and ulcerative colitis, the two main forms of IBD, are typically treated only after symptoms appear, when the gut has already been damaged. But scientists found that the immune system sends warning signals up to a decade before diagnosis, paving the way for potentially earlier detection and even prevention. Continue reading...

data.title: At 7, she was 'gifted' to Queen Victoria; 176 years later, her descendant revisits her life
data.description: In 1850, a seven-year-old African girl named Aina was presented to Queen Victoria as a diplomatic 'gift' after losing her family and spending two years in captivity. Renamed Sarah Forbes Bonetta, she grew up under royal protection but faced restrictions on her freedom. Now, 176 years later, a new biography is examining her life, while her great-great-grandson, Bayo Randle, reflects on her struggles, achievements and complicated relationship with the British monarchy.

data.title: Camera giant Kodak operated a uranium-based nuclear device beneath its laboratory
data.description: For 31 years, Kodak operated a uranium-based research device beneath its Rochester laboratory, using it to examine materials and detect impurities. Installed in 1975 and shut down in 2006, the machine attracted public attention in 2012 because it contained highly enriched uranium. A new Popular Mechanics report explains how the device produced neutrons through nuclear fission but could not sustain a chain reaction independently, making it different from a conventional nuclear reactor.

data.title: Michigan to ban untreated firewood from January 2027 over risk of 140-plus pests and diseases
data.description: Michigan will ban untreated, uncertified firewood from entering the state starting January 1, 2027, to prevent the spread of more than 140 plant pests and diseases. The restriction will apply to travellers, campers and businesses, with exemptions for certified, heat-treated wood and certain other wood products. Authorities will focus on public awareness in 2027, while repeat violations could attract fines of $1,000 to $10,000 from 2028.

Meanwhile, trade imbalance concerns ignite dialogue among trading partners seeking sustainable solutions.

data.title: Women out of work, millions hungry: Afghanistan's lost 5 yrs under Taliban
data.description: Since the Taliban's resurgence in Afghanistan, women's rights and access to education have suffered dramatically. Millions of girls are now prohibited from secondary and higher education, leading to dire social repercussions. In addition, food insecurity is rampant, affecting approximately 19.2 million individuals. The healthcare available has also significantly declined, obstructing women's ability to obtain necessary medical assistance. The overall humanitarian crisis continues to worsen, deeply affecting Afghan families' daily lives.

data.title: Flowers, roast pork and paper ingots: families keep Chung Yeung traditions alive

data.title: Debate de Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro é marcado por Vorcaro e Luchsinger
data.description: Lula (PT) e Flávio Bolsonaro ( PL ) ficaram frente a frente pela primeira vez neste domingo (18), no debate da Band , a uma semana do segundo turno. O encontro começou com segurança pública e economia, mas foi tomado por uma troca de acusações envolvendo Daniel Vorcaro e Roberta Luchsinger. O presidente cobrou o voto do senador contra a licença-maternidade e os R$ 134 milhões de Daniel Vorcaro, ex-dono do Banco Master . Flávio sem responder diretamente aos questionamentos, questionou a relação de Lulinha com lobista Roberta Luchsinger. O debate teve ainda discussão sobre o voto dos presidiários e o "malandro carioca", que Flávio transformou em solidariedade ao Rio. Leia mais (10/19/2026 - 00h36)

data.title: Pauta das armas não pode ficar fora da vitrine
data.description: Em 28 de outubro de 2025, durante a Operação Contenção nos complexos da Penha e do Alemão, no Rio de Janeiro , o Comando Vermelho sustentou 14 horas de tiroteio contra milhares de policiais. Para isso, precisou de muita munição. A pesquisa recém-lançada "De onde vem o tiro?" , do Instituto Sou da Paz , analisou 31.699 cartuchos de fuzil apreendidos com a facção entre 2018 e 2025 e encontrou um dado incômodo: 40,9% eram de fabricação brasileira. Pouco mais da metade desses cartuchos nacionais trazia códigos de rastreabilidade de compras institucionais, ou seja, adquiridos por Forças Armadas ou polícias e, em algum momento, saiu do controle do Estado. Leia mais (10/18/2026 - 22h00)

data.title: Nový rok 1968? Nepokoje vstoupí do historie, jsou síla i na Francii
data.description: Francií otřásají masové protesty. Už zase. Dějiny páté republiky jsou protkány bezpočtem vln demonstrací a stávek, jež už se otiskly do DNA země. Jaké místo zaujmou nynější nepokoje vedle bouří května 1968, protestů na pařížských předměstích v době, kdy byl Nicolas Sarkozy ministrem vnitra, či zloby takzvaných žlutých vest?
data.translatedTitle: Nový rok 1968? Nepokoje vstoupí do historie, jsou síla i na Francii

Jaké místo zaujmou nynější nepokoje vedle bouří května 1968, protestů na pařížských předměstích v době, kdy byl Nicolas Sarkozy ministrem vnitra, či zloby takzvaných žlutých vest?

data.title: Volkswagen plánuje zmrazit mzdy do roku 2030, týká se to i Škody, tvrdí odboráři
data.description: Automobilový koncern Volkswagen plánuje do roku 2030 zmrazit mzdy svých více než 660 tisíců zaměstnanců. V tiskové zprávě to v pondělí uvedl německý odborový svaz IG Metall. Volkswagen odmítl informaci, kterou dříve přinesl i deník Süddeutsche Zeitung, komentovat. Součástí koncernu Volkswagen je i česká Škoda Auto, která má zhruba 36 500 zaměstnanců včetně agenturních.

data.title: Servala někdo vypustil úmyslně nebo ukradl, myslí si majitelé zookoutku
data.description: Servala, který v polovině minulého pracovního týdne zmizel ze zookoutku ve Vápovicích na Jihlavsku, zřejmě někdo úmyslně vypustil. A nebo ho dokonce ukradl. Myslí si to provozovatelé zařízení. I tyto možnosti prověřuje policie. Zvíře se zatím nenašlo. Zookoutek prosí o spolupráci při hledání veřejnost.

data.title: Kladno povede dosavadní koalice plus ODS, primátorem zůstane Volf
data.description: Po devíti dnech vyjednávání je jasno o novém vedení radnice v Kladně. Největší středočeské město povede v příštích čtyřech letech koalice Volba pro Kladno (VPK), ANO a ODS. Na základě výsledků komunálních voleb dosavadní dvojblok VPK a ANO rozšíří občanští demokraté.

data.title: Macinka odmítl celoevropské omezení víz pro Rusy. Většina zemí je proti, tvrdí
data.description: Česko nepodpořilo finský návrh na omezení vstupu Rusů do Evropské unie, podle serveru Seznam Zprávy o tom rozhodl ministr zahraničí Petr Macinka (Motoristé). Česko podobné omezení samo uplatňuje, Rusové ale mohou do Česka vstoupit z okolních zemí. Podle Finska ruské sabotáže a další hybridní operace ohrožují EU, unie by proto měla změnit vízovou politiku vůči Rusku.

data.title: Sucho na Slapech odkrylo i spoustu odpadků. Lidé se o prázdninách mohou zapojit do úklidu
data.description: Lidé se příští týden o podzimních prázdninách mohou zapojit do úklidu Slapské přehrady. Dlouhotrvající sucho odkrylo nejen obrovské množství vzácných škeblí, ale také obrovské množství odpadků. Velký úklid se uskuteční od 28. října do 1. listopadu.

data.title: Olomouc už zná nové vedení. Primátorem se stane Zelenka, koalice má pět stran
data.description: Dny licitování jsou u konce - město Olomouc už zná svoji novou vládu na nadcházející čtyři roky. Ve vedení magistrátu končí hnutí ANO, které sice ovládlo komunální volby, ale přesouvá se do opozice. Novou koalici tvoří hnutí STAN, ProOlomouc, KDU-ČSL, spOLečně a Milujeme Olomouc. Primátorem se stane lídr Starostů Marek Zelenka.

data.title: ANO, STAN a PRO PLZEŇ podepsaly v Plzni koaliční smlouvu, mají pohodlnou většinu
data.description: Všech 34 zastupitelů za ANO, STAN a PRO PLZEŇ s podporou lidovců podepsalo v Plzni koaliční smlouvu. V zastupitelstvu se 47 členy má koalice pohodlnou většinu. Koalice se dohodla, že sníží počet radních z dosavadních 11 na devět, ze 13 na 11 klesne také počet poradních komisí.

data.title: Tragédie při závodech. Motokrosař se na Opavsku těžce zranil, v nemocnici zemřel

data.title: Zlomené obratle, hrozba amputace prstu. Izrael vyšetřuje útok osadníků na fotografku
data.description: Izraelská policie zadržela osm podezřelých v rámci vyšetřování víkendových násilností na okupovaném Západním břehu, mezi nimiž byly i útoky na americkou fotoreportérku a evropské diplomaty. Agentura Reuters podotýká, že stíhání izraelských osadníků je vzácné. Policie podezřelé neidentifikovala ani nesdělila, z čeho je viní.

data.title: Úřady podcenily přípravu, přiznal Macron. Demisi ministra kvůli násilnostem nepřijal
data.description: Francouzský ministr vnitra Laurent Nuňez podal demisi kvůli víkendovým násilnostem v ulicích měst. Prezident Emmanuel Macron ji nepřijal, uznal však, že úřady podcenily přípravu, a vyzval ministra k přijetí nových opatření proti násilníkům, uvedl podle agentury AFP Elysejský palác. Podle pondělního vyjádření ministra spravedlnosti Géralda Darmanina se na násilnostech podílela řada lidí dobře známých policii a desítky z nich skončily ve vazbě. V Paříži pokračovaly násilnosti i v neděli a v noci na dnešek, vyrabovány byly nejméně tři desítky obchodů, uvedl starosta Emmanuel Grégoire.

data.title: Vymíráme. Zachrání nás penze v 73 letech i vyšší daně pro bezdětné, radí ekonomové
data.description: Postupný odchod do penze až v 73 letech, vyšší zdanění bezdětných a podpora pečujícího rodiče 800 tisíc korun během prvních dvou let života dítěte. Ekonomové Miroslav Singer a Aleš Rod v Rozstřelu na iDNES.cz představili návrhy institutu Solvo, jak čelit stárnutí populace a usnadnit zakládání rodin. Důchodový věk 73 let jejich model předpokládá v horizontu let 2065 až 2070, podmínkou je podle nich prodloužení života ve zdraví.

data.title: Čínská ekonomika zrychlila růst na 4,5 procenta, překonala veškerá očekávání
data.description: Čínská ekonomika ve třetím čtvrtletí meziročně vzrostla na 4,5 procenta. Tempo růstu tak zrychlilo ze 4,3 procenta v předchozím čtvrtletí a překonalo očekávání analytiků. Ekonomiku podpořil silný vývoz, čínští spotřebitelé však zůstávají při utrácení opatrní. Vyplývá to z údajů, které dnes zveřejnil čínský statistický úřad.

data.title: Vyhýbejte se demonstracím ve Francii, doporučilo Čechům ministerstvo
data.description: Ministerstvo zahraničí doporučuje Čechům ve Francii vyhýbat se veškerým demonstracím, pochodům a veřejným shromážděním. Uvedlo to ve zprávě pro české občany zaregistrované v dobrovolném cestovatelském systému Drozd. Především velká francouzská města zažívají vlnu protestů a demonstrací, kvůli kterým se podle české diplomacie zhoršila bezpečnostní situace v zemi.

data.title: Co Putin na Trumpa má? ptá se Pelosiová po pozastavení protiruských sankcí
data.description: Bývalá předsedkyně americké Sněmovny reprezentantů Nancy Pelosiová opět ostře zkritizovala Donalda Trumpa. Připomněla svoji větu, že v jeho případě „všechny cesty vedou k Putinovi“. Reagovala na Trumpovo zrušení nových protiruských sankcí. Krok označila za kapitulaci. Rozhodnutí Bílého domu odsoudil i ukrajinský prezident Volodymyr Zelenskyj.

data.title: Malá, nebo velká koalice? O pozici primátora politici ve Zlíně zatím nejednají
data.description: Ve Zlíně se řeší podoba nové koalice, která povede město po komunálních volbách. data.title: Letadlo z Tel Avivu do Vídně nouzově přistálo v Sofii. Doprovázely ho stíhačky
data.description: Civilní dopravní letadlo na lince z Tel Avivu do Vídně muselo v neděli večer nouzově přistát v bulharském hlavním městě Sofii kvůli výhrůžce bombovým útokem, oznámila bulharská televize BNT. data.title: Rozruch v Ústí. Suverén voleb mluví o rušení obvodů, radnice se chtějí bránit
data.description: Vítězná koalice Jedno Ústí, která bude vládnout na ústeckém magistrátu bez dalších partnerů, debatuje o možném zrušení obvodů. Například starostka Neštěmic Yveta Tomková (Vaše Ústí) v reakci na to uvedla, že neštěmický obvod nedá. Pravděpodobný budoucí primátor Tomáš Vohryzka řekl, že nic není rozhodnuto, rušení obvodů je jedna z možností, jak ušetřit v rozpočtu.

data.title: Řidiče postihla zástava srdce, naboural do rodinného domu. Zemřel v nemocnici
data.description: Řidič nákladního vozidla v pražské Letňanské ulici v neděli nečekaně vyjel na zahradu rodinného pozemku a naboural do domu. Podle záchranářů muž nezvládl řízení kvůli náhlé zástavě srdce. S oživováním pomáhali svědci. Kontinuální resuscitace však selhaly a muž později v nemocnici zemřel.

data.title: Čeští vojáci na hraně konfliktu. Televizní série ukáže, co obnáší obrana svobody
data.description: Jak vypadá půlroční mise českých vojáků na východním křídle NATO? Šestidílná dokumentární série „Provedu! Cena za svobodu“ režiséra Benjamina Tučka zavede diváky na přísně střeženou základnu v litevské Rukle. Ukáže nejen vojenský výcvik, ale také psychický tlak, odloučení od rodin a proměňující se bezpečnostní situaci v Evropě. Vznese i otázky bezpečnosti naší země v případě konfliktu Ruska se Severoatlantickou aliancí.

data.title: Nepokoje se z Francie přesunuly i do Itálie. V Miláně hořelo u katedrály, zatkli 200 lidí
data.description: V centru Milána se o víkendu střetli mladí lidé s policií. Podle agentur ministr vnitra Matteo Piantedosi v neděli večer oznámil, že policie zadržela na 200 lidí. Většině zadržených nebylo ještě 18 let. Milánská katedrála musela předčasně ukončit prohlídky turistů. Na pondělí italská premiérka Giorgia Meloniová svolala radu pro veřejný pořádek. Zatím nejsou informace o zraněných.

data.title: Putin navrhl Trumpovi summit o Ukrajině bez Ukrajiny, schůzka by byla v Číně
data.description: Ruský prezident Vladimir Putin navrhl uspořádat příští měsíc summit s americkým prezidentem Donaldem Trumpem a čínským vůdcem Si Ťin-pchingem, jehož cílem by bylo vyjednat ukončení více než čtyři roky trvajícího konfliktu na Ukrajině za podmínek výhodných pro Moskvu. Americký ministr zahraničí Marco Rubio Ukrajině a Rusku vzkázal, že by se měly soustředit na ukončení války.

data.title: Požár na kanadské vojenské základně usmrtil čtyři vojáky a dalších 19 zranil
data.description: Při požáru, který v kanadské provincii Alberta připravil o život čtyři kanadské vojáky, bylo hospitalizováno 39 lidí, z toho 19 je v kritickém stavu, uvedly úřady podle tiskových agentur. Kanadský premiér Mark Carney označil neštěstí za jednu z nejhorších tragédií, jakou kdy zažila kanadská armáda na domácí půdě v době míru. Nařídil spustit vlajky na federálních budovách po celé zemi na půl žerdi k uctění památky obětí.

data.title: Novo julgamento de Sócrates. "Abriu o teatro do absurdo"
data.description: Deveria ter tido início esta segunda-feira o julgamento por branqueamento de capitais, num caso que resultou da decisão instrutória do processo Operação Marquês, datada de 2021.  O início do julgamento foi adiado para 30 de outubro, para que o tribunal possa decidir questões prévias que podem pôr em causa a realização do julgamento. O antigo primeiro-ministro fala de "absurdo".

O início do julgamento foi adiado para 30 de outubro, para que o tribunal possa decidir questões prévias que podem pôr em causa a realização do julgamento. O antigo primeiro-ministro fala de "absurdo".

data.description: Às segundas-feiras sucedem-se as alterações nos preços dos combustíveis. Um sobe e desce constante que se deve principalmente a dois conflitos: Ucrânia e Médio Oriente. According to the General Authority for Statistics, intracity traveler numbers jumped to 145.4 million from 31.1 million in 2024, an increase of 368 percent. data.title: Macron urges calm as France counts the cost of worst unrest in years
data.description: PARIS/LIMOGES: President Emmanuel Macron appealed for calm on Sunday, a day after France suffered one of its worst days of unrest in years, with thousands arrested and shops looted or damaged after protests over high prices and declining public services. Fresh clashes broke out in Paris and Marseille, where riot police intervened to prevent attempts to ransack businesses. Nationwide demonstrations had erupted into riots on Saturday, with a town hall torched, shops pillaged and buildings covered

data.title: Why the Houthis could pose a greater threat than Al-Qaeda and Daesh
data.description: CAIRO: The Houthis, Al-Qaeda and Daesh come from sharply different religious traditions. The Yemeni militia is rooted in a hard-line interpretation of Zaydi Shiism, while Al-Qaeda and Daesh emerged from extremist movements. Their doctrinal disagreements are profound, and they have fought each other on the ground. Yet the differences can obscure a more consequential question: Which poses the greater long-term threat to Yemen and the wider region? The answer cannot be measured solely by the number

data.title: Arsenal snatch late win to keep pressure on Man City as Man Utd held
data.description: LONDON: Arsenal struck late to beat Nottingham Forest and keep the pressure on Premier League leaders Manchester City on Sunday, while struggling Manchester United dropped more points in a draw at Leeds. The Gunners faced Forest a day after pacesetters City celebrated a seventh win in seven games at home to Ipswich — shrugging off the fallout from the club’s guilty verdict for serious financial irregularities. Defending champions Arsenal huffed and puffed against Oliver Glasner’s struggling side

data.title: Cameroun : Hiram Samuel Iyodi annonce sa candidature aux élections municipales et législatives 2027
data.description: © DR Le président national du Mouvement patriotique pour la prospérité du peuple (MP3) a annoncé le dimanche 18 octobre 2026 qu’il se présentera aux prochaines élections dans le Littoral. Après la première tentative infructueuse à la présidentielle du 12 octobre 2025 (0,40% des suffrages), Hiram Samuel Iyodi entend se lancer à la course pour les législatives et les municipales. L’ancien candidat à la présidentielle a fait l’annonce le 18 octobre 2026 au cours de l’émission L’Arène sur Canal 2 International. Le plus jeune candidat en lice pour le fauteuil présidentiel en 2025 indique qu’il se présenterait dans la région du Littoral où la population l’a le plus voté lors de la dernière élection. Sans donner plus de précisions sur la commune ou le département où il va se présenter, il laisse entendre qu’il pourra le faire dans l’une des circonscriptions électorales de la ville de Douala ou de la ville d’Edéa. Par ailleurs, le parti politique dont il est président va présenter des candidats presque dans l’ensemble des grandes aires du pays. La précision à ce sujet est que le MP3 va se présenter dans 10 circonscriptions électorales en ce qui concerne les élections législatives. Ce qui correspond à une trentaine de candidats. Quant aux élections municipales, le parti compte investir des candidats dans 40 communes du pays. D’après les explications de l’homme politique, le choix de ces circonscriptions découle de l’étude des réalités du terrain et de l’implantation du parti. Les investitures de candidats ciblent ainsi les localités où la formation politique est sûre de pouvoir gagner la bataille électorale. Là où les responsables locaux du parti ont démontré leur capacité de pouvoir mobiliser la population et amener les électeurs à concrétiser leur adhésion et leur sympathie au parti en élisant ses candidats. Ce serait ainsi une première pour Hiram Samuel Iyodi qui explique avoir voulu se présenter aux élections locales et législatives avant la présidentielle de 2025. Ses intentions étaient de se lancer à la course lors des élections municipales et législatives qui devaient se dérouler en 2025. Mais le report de ces élections a entrainé le retard de ses ambitions de devenir maire ou député de la nation. A présent qu’il veut se présenter après la présidentielle de 2025, son parcours politique va ressembler à celui de Cabral Libii. Plus jeune candidat à la présidentielle de 2018 sous la bannière du parti Univers, Cabral Libii s’est présenté aux législatives de 2020 avec le Pcrn. A l’issue des élections, il a été élu député de la nation avant de poursuivre son combat politique. En 2025, Hiram Samuel Iyodi est candidat à la présidentielle investi par le FDC. En 2027, il compte se présenter sous la bannière du MP3. Et il entend rassembler tous les moyens possibles pour que le parti atteigne ses objectifs. Dans ce sens, l’homme politique n’exclut pas les concertations et rapprochements avec d’autres partis politiques d’opposition comme l’OMP ou encore le MRC. Cet article Cameroun : Hiram Samuel Iyodi annonce sa candidature aux élections municipales et législatives 2027 est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: La peste des petits ruminants décime près de 200 chèvres à Idjwi, les autorités appellent à l’aide
data.description: Au moins 191 chèvres sont mortes de la peste des petits ruminants (PPR) entre le 6 juin et le 6 octobre 2026 dans la chefferie de Rubenga, au nord du territoire d’Idjwi, au Sud-Kivu. Face à la propagation de cette maladie animale, l’inspection territoriale de l’Agriculture, de la Pêche et de l’Élevage appelle à une intervention vétérinaire urgente et recommande des mesures de prévention aux habitants.

data.title: The stadium is full, the nation is waiting
data.description:
A single aerial photograph of the Accra Sports Stadium on the night of 17 October 2026 tells a story that no policy document has managed to tell as clearly: Ghana does not lack people who are willing to gather, to give, to wait, and to believe. What it lacks are
institutions that young people trust enough to gather for. This article reads the ShattaFest crowd through the lenses of crowd psychology, the sociology of religion and development economics, names where the State and the Church have fallen short, and proposes a practical agenda for redirecting this extraordinary energy toward national development.

data.description: Les habitants d'Antananarivo subissent une nouvelle vague de délestages. Depuis plusieurs jours, de nombreux quartiers de la capitale connaissent des interruptions d'électricité, parfois plus longues que les horaires annoncés par la Jirama. Cette situation intervient alors que la compagnie nationale prévoit également des travaux d'entretien du réseau du 16 au 22 octobre. data.title: El Surfacen cubano amplía sus potencialidades terapéuticas en asma y otras enfermedades respiratorias
data.description: Más de 30 años después de su obtención por un equipo de especialistas del Centro Nacional de Sanidad Agropecuaria (Censa), y de emplearse en unidades de cuidados intensivos neonatales para tratar el distrés respiratorio, el producto cubano Surfacen amplía sus potencialidades terapéuticas en asma bronquial y otras enfermedades respiratorias. Así lo demuestran los resultados de un proyecto encabezado por la doctora en Ciencias Farmacéuticas Odalys Blanco Hidalgo, Investigadora Titular del Censa, en alianza con la Universidad Complutense de Madrid, líderes en investigaciones biofísicas y farmacéuticas de los surfactantes pulmonares a nivel internacional. Titulado Estudios biofísicos y farmacológicos de Surfacen: potencialidades terapéuticas en enfermedades por daño pulmonar e inflamación, el trabajo mereció el Premio Nacional de la Academia de Ciencias de Cuba 2025 y contó con la colaboración de diferentes instituciones cubanas. Consultada por Granma, la doctora Blanco Hidalgo explicó que se trata de un fármaco de origen natural obtenido a partir del lavado broncoalveolar de origen porcino, cuyo empleo a lo largo de más de tres décadas contribuyó de manera significativa a reducir la mortalidad infantil en recién nacidos prematuros, que, al no tener la suficiente madurez en los pulmones, estaban impedidos de producir el surfactante pulmonar endógeno requerido para la respiración. “Nuestra investigación  » The post El Surfacen cubano amplía sus potencialidades terapéuticas en asma y otras enfermedades respiratorias first appeared on Cubadebate .

data.title: El ‘jet’ de las zonas francas y el avión rezagado de la economía nacional

data.title: Kylie Jenner debuta en el Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show y luce el "Fantasy Bra"
data.description: California. Resulta que Victoria’s Secret guardaba un gran secreto sobre las celebridades que participarían como modelos este año. Este domingo, Kylie Jenner sorprendió a los asistentes al Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show 2026 al desfilar, por primera vez en su historia, para la icónica firma de lencería. Llevó puesto el primer "Fantasy Bra" de la marca; una pieza que, según el diseñador Jacob Arabo —de la firma Jacob & Co.—, es " el Fantasy Bra más caro jamás creado ". Solo el diamante amarillo central está valorado en 22 millones de dólares, según el joyero. El diseño incluye, además, diamantes con "todos los tipos de talla existentes", tales como pera, corazón, redonda, ovalada, marquesa, entre otras. Su novio, el actor Timothée Chalamet , estuvo presente entre el público para apoyarla, sentado junto a la madre de ella, Kris Jenner , y la pareja de esta, Corey Gamble . Aunque la fundadora de Kylie Cosmetics está acostumbrada a protagonizar sesiones de fotos muy sexis, no es habitual verla sobre una pasarela. Recientemente, fue la encargada de cerrar el desfile de Coperni en 2024, celebrado en Disneyland París, luciendo un elegante vestido de gala sin tirantes. Su debut en una pasarela se remonta a 2011, para Abbey Dawn, la antigua firma de Avril Lavigne. Asimismo, en 2013, desfiló junto a su hermana, Kendall Jenner, tanto para la marca Sherri Hill como para el evento "Red Dress Collection" de la campaña "The Heart Truth". Mira el video: .

data.title: Buba López recibe noticia clave y Real España anuncia nuevo proyecto
data.description: Luis Aurelio López afrontará un largo camino donde la meta final es volver a defender la portería de su querido Real España y esto luego de la fractura de tibia que sufrió en el último clásico ante Olimpia . El guardián de 33 años fue operado exitosamente y es el doctor del cuadro aurinegro , Emid Salinas quien  dio detalles del proceso de recuperación que afrontará. “El proceso de una fractura va por etapas, la inicial es cuando se procede a inmovilizar al paciente y evitar que haga cargas importantes en la zona afectada y después de la segunda o tercera semana se inicia con los trabajos de movilidad”, expresó el profesional que le presta los servicios médicos a los catedráticos desde hace dos años. Salimos comentó que esperan que Buba vuelva a los terrenos de juego dentro de 4 a 6 meses. ¿Qué procede para Buba López tras su lamentable lesión? Luis sufrió una fractura del tercio distal de la tibia izquierda e inmediatamente activamos los protocolos de emergencia y lo trasladamos a un centro médico donde pudimos constatar la fractura.  El procedimiento quirúrgico se realizó en San Pedro Sula con uno de los especialistas más prestigiosos de la ciudad, el doctor Juan José Sánchez. La operación duró 1:20 minutos aproximadamente. Describiendo superficialmente se hizo una fijación con un clavo intramedular bloqueado. ¿Cuánto tiempo estará fuera de las canchas? El proceso de recuperación comienza en dos semanas y va tener una duración de 4 a 6 meses . Cada paciente es diferente , pero ese es el estimado que tenemos en cuanto al tiempo de recuperación. ¿En qué consiste la recuperación? El proceso de una fractura va por etapas, la inicial es cuando se procede a inmovilizar al paciente y evitar que haga cargas importantes en la zona afectada y después de la segunda o tercera semana se inicia con los trabajos de movilidad. Luego hay tres o cuatro etapas más que debe cumplir para ya estar apto para los trabajos en cancha. -Clinica del Real España- ¿Habrá una clínica para las personas por parte de Real España? Esta clínica estará ubicada en el centro de la ciudad, estamos próximos a dar más información. La clínica de medicina deportiva tendrá servicios especializados que se le dan a los jugares de alto rendimiento y estará abierta al público para poder darle un servicio especializado.

data.title: Presidente Asfura viajará a Italia para fortalecer relaciones diplomáticas y promover la inversión
data.description: El presidente de Honduras, Nasry Asfura, viajará la próxima semana a Italia y a la Santa Sede con el objetivo de fortalecer las relaciones diplomáticas, promover oportunidades comerciales y atraer inversiones al país. Mireya Agüero , la secretaria ​​​​​​de Relaciones Exteriores y Cooperación Internacional, dio a conocer los detalles de la gira oficial y confirmó que el mandatario se reunirá con el presidente italiano, Sergio Mattarella , en el Palacio del Quirinal, en Roma. Durante el encuentro, ambos países buscarán identificar nuevas oportunidades de colaboración y fortalecer las relaciones bilaterales. La agenda también contempla la presentación de las fortalezas productivas de Honduras para despertar el interés de empresarios italianos en posibles proyectos de inversión. Como parte de la gira, Asfura participará en una reunión con representantes del sector empresarial en el norte de Italia. Asimismo, tiene previsto sostener conversaciones con representantes de la Organización de las Naciones Unidas para la Alimentación y la Agricultura ( FAO ) para explorar proyectos conjuntos y ampliar la cooperación en áreas de interés para Honduras. La agenda presidencial también incluye una visita al Vaticano, donde el gobernante hondureño se reunirá con el secretario de Estado de la Santa Sede, el cardenal Pietro Parolin. Además, está prevista la firma de un acuerdo entre Honduras y el Vaticano para fortalecer los vínculos institucionales y diplomáticos. Otro de los puntos del itinerario será un encuentro con hondureños residentes en Italia. La reunión permitirá conocer las principales preocupaciones de la comunidad migrante y abordar posibles para mejorar la atención y el acompañamiento que reciben desde Honduras. Agüero destacó que la misión diplomática busca presentar tanto las necesidades del país como las oportunidades que ofrece para establecer alianzas internacionales. La funcionaria también subrayó la importancia de aprovechar estos espacios para promover los intereses nacionales y abrir nuevos canales de colaboración. Al concluir la visita, la Cancillería hondureña dará seguimiento a los compromisos y acercamientos alcanzados durante las reuniones, con el propósito de convertir las gestiones diplomáticas en iniciativas que contribuyan al desarrollo económico y social del país.

data.title: Tabla de LaLiga: Real Madrid acecha al Barcelona previo al clásico y así está la distancia
data.description: El Real Madrid no tuvo problemas para imponer su autoridad y este domingo recetó una contundente goleada de 4-1 al Sevilla , en duelo correspondiente a la jornada 10 de LaLiga de España , disputado en el estadio Santiago Bernabéu. El conjunto merengue respondió a la presión en la lucha por el liderato y consiguió tres puntos importantes ante su afición. Con un fútbol efectivo y pegada en los momentos decisivos, los dirigidos por José Mourinho resolvieron el compromiso gracias a un doblete del francés Kylian Mbappé , una auténtica obra de arte del turco Arda Güler y otro tanto de Diomande.. Con este triunfo, el Real Madrid escala al tercer lugar de la tabla de posiciones de LaLiga, al alcanzar los 21 puntos después de diez jornadas disputadas. El liderato le pertenece al Barcelona , que suma 27 unidades, mientras que el Atlético de Madrid ocupa la segunda posición con 22 puntos. De esta manera, los merengues consiguieron una victoria importante antes de afrontar uno de los compromisos más esperados de la temporada. Aunque lograron recortar distancias respecto a sus perseguidores, todavía tienen trabajo por delante para acercarse al primer puesto, actualmente en manos de su máximo rival. Cabe señalar que, en la próxima jornada de la Liga española, el Real Madrid visitará el Spotify Camp Nou para enfrentarse al Barcelona en una nueva edición del clásico que paraliza al mundo del fútbol. El encuentro promete emociones, debido a la rivalidad histórica entre ambos clubes y a la importancia de los puntos en la lucha por el campeonato. Los azulgranas buscarán defender su liderato ante su afición, mientras que los madridistas intentarán dar un golpe de autoridad y reducir la diferencia en la clasificación. data.title: Caen dos presuntos miembros de banda “Satanás” con supuesta droga en Catacamas
data.description: Catacamas, Olancho. Dos hombres señalados preliminarmente como supuestos integrantes de la banda delictiva “Satanás” fueron detenidos por agentes de la Policía Nacional en el barrio La Cruz, en el municipio de Catacamas, departamento de Olancho, por suponerlos responsables del delito de tráfico de drogas. Los detenidos fueron identificados como Marco Tulio Ramos Erazo , de 27 años, originario de Catacamas y de oficio mecánico automotriz, y Juan Ramón Santos Erazo , de 25 años, oriundo de Santa María del Real, Olancho. Ambos tienen su domicilio en el barrio La Cruz, según el informe policial. La captura se realizó la noche del sábado 17 de octubre, luego de que la Policía recibiera una alerta sobre la presunta venta y el consumo de sustancias ilícitas en la vía pública de ese sector. Al llegar al barrio, los funcionarios identificaron a varias personas y requirieron a los dos hombres, quienes presuntamente intentaron darse a la fuga al percatarse de la presencia policial. Durante el registro personal, los agentes encontraron 23 envoltorios con polvo blanco, presumiblemente cocaína, además de dos bolsas que contenían hierba seca, supuestamente marihuana, según el reporte de las autoridades. Los indicios fueron decomisados como parte del procedimiento investigativo para determinar la naturaleza de las sustancias y documentar la presunta participación de los detenidos en actividades relacionadas con el tráfico de drogas. Según los registros policiales, uno de los hombres cuenta con antecedentes por una detención relacionada con el delito de tráfico de drogas en julio de 2025. También registra otras incidencias relacionadas con el decomiso de vehículos y faltas a la Ley de Policía y Convivencia Social. Tras la detención, los dos hombres fueron trasladados a las instalaciones de la Dirección Policial de Investigaciones en Catacamas, junto con las sustancias decomisadas, para continuar con las diligencias correspondientes. Posteriormente, ambos serán puestos a disposición de las autoridades competentes para que se determine el procedimiento legal que corresponda por el supuesto delito de tráfico de drogas. La Policía mantiene las investigaciones para establecer si los sospechosos estarían vinculados con otras actividades ilícitas en el municipio de Catacamas y determinar el alcance de sus presuntas operaciones.
