data.title: Constructor announces progress at Romania’s first green energy sports arena
data.description: Work on the “Nicolae Dobrin” stadium in Pitești, the first sports arena in Romania to operate exclusively on green energy,  is progressing, according to information provided by the company Construcții Erbașu. Work to rebuild this stadium began in March 2026. According to the National Investment Company (CNI), the future stadium will have 15,200 seats and host top-level sporting competitions. The project will include modern facilities for athletes, spectators, the media and officials, alongside complementary spaces, parking facilities and outdoor landscaping. https://www.facebook.com/constructiierbasu/posts/pfbid09kGF1kFtboMUy2k4fDGbW3h9YF6ezy39jqTsJY4zWhEQg5S2H6pJA7mDtEfetEQ7l?locale=ro_RO “The ‘Nicolae Dobrin’ stadium in Pitești is increasingly taking on the final shape that has so far only been presented in renderings. We have already installed the prefabricated beams at the North Stand, and we are now preparing the area for the seating tiers,” the constructor said in a press release. The stadium includes a children's and youth training centre and training facilities for related sports (wrestling, boxing, judo and karate), offices, parking facilities and commercial areas. In total, the facilities will span a total floor area of 71,000 sqm. The constructor has 3 years to complete the project, but progress is already visible. The slab above the parking area is 80% complete, the ground-floor columns have reached 98%, and the plumbing and rainwater drainage systems on this level are 85% complete, the same source added. “At the same time, we are working on the floor slabs in the North Stand and East Stand promenade areas and preparing the ground-floor flooring,” Construcții Erbașu added.

data.title: Romanian president promulgates law on 401(k)-like personal retirement account
data.description: The law was adopted in September in Parliament. Nicușor Dan has now promulgated the project, which regulates the legal framework for retirement accounts, called Savings and Investment Accounts (CEI), modeled after accounts similar to the 401(k) and IRA (Individual Retirement Account) in the US. The money in these accounts will be able to be invested in shares, bonds, investment funds, and other eligible financial instruments, traded on regulated markets in the European Union or on equivalent markets in member states of the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD), Economedia.ro reported. The project excludes direct investments in derivative financial instruments, with certain exceptions for investment funds that use them to track an index or to hedge risks. One of the main advantages proposed is the tax exemption for income and gains obtained from investments within CEI accounts. These will not be included in the calculation base for income tax and mandatory social contributions during the period of holding the account. Also, dividends received in these accounts will be tax-exempt.

data.title: Astorium Nest joins North Bucharest Investments' portfolio as part of its residential diversification strategy
data.description: The project will comprise 55 apartments, with prices starting at €76,464 plus VAT and an estimated completion date in 2027. The expanded collaboration strengthens the commercial partnership between the two companies and forms part of NBI's strategy to diversify its residential portfolio. Located in Bucharest's District 3, the development will feature one-, two-, and three-room apartments across two residential buildings, each comprising a ground floor and three upper floors. The project is primarily aimed at owner-occupiers, in a market where purchasing decisions are increasingly shaped by price, layout, accessibility, and quality of living. The expansion of the partnership with Astorium comes as North Bucharest Investments continues to adapt its commercial strategy to changing buyer demographics. According to Vlad Musteata, approximately 70 to 80% of current demand comes from buyers purchasing properties for their own use, prompting a stronger focus on competitively priced developments, diverse apartment configurations, and amenities tailored to residents' needs. "The residential market is entering a new phase in which success is no longer defined solely by development volumes, but by the ability to respond to genuine market demand. We are seeing a growing proportion of owner-occupiers, which is driving us to diversify both our portfolio and our developer partnerships. Astorium Nest is part of this strategy. For us, the next stage of growth is about scaling our operations, expanding our presence across residential segments, and strengthening our sales and distribution capabilities." said Vlad Musteata, Founder & CEO of North Bucharest Investments. North Bucharest Investments currently works with more than 80 developers and represents a portfolio of over 100 residential projects, approximately 40% of which are marketed on an exclusive basis. Astorium Nest further expands the development portfolio of Astorium, which already includes Astorium Life, Astorium Garden, and Astorium Boutique. The new development comprises 55 apartments across two residential buildings, T2 and T3, each featuring a ground floor and three upper floors. The residential concept places particular emphasis on functional layouts, privacy, and the integration of green spaces. Ground-floor apartments benefit from private gardens, while the development also features landscaped communal green areas for residents. Situated in the Theodor Pallady area, Astorium Nest offers convenient access to the commercial, educational, and healthcare infrastructure of eastern Bucharest. The development is located near the Anghel Saligny and Nicolae Teclu metro stations, as well as major retail destinations, including Auchan Pallady and IKEA, alongside schools and healthcare facilities. With its boutique scale, variety of apartment configurations, and integration of private outdoor spaces, Astorium Nest is designed to appeal to both first-time buyers and families seeking new homes in an emerging residential area. "Astorium Nest reflects the direction in which we are developing the Astorium brand: thoughtfully designed residential projects where construction quality, functionality, and residents' comfort take priority. Our ambition was to offer more than new apartments. We wanted to create a residential environment that brings together privacy, green spaces, and a high standard of living. The 55 apartments have been designed around the real needs of buyers, and Astorium Nest reinforces our commitment to delivering competitive developments that create long-term value. Our partnership with North Bucharest Investments strengthens the project's commercial positioning and provides access to a broader network of potential buyers." said Ulas Dilmac, Owner of Astorium. The addition of Astorium Nest marks a further step in the ongoing collaboration between North Bucharest Investments and Astorium, at a time when real estate developers are placing increasing importance on effective sales strategies, access to qualified buyers, and greater predictability throughout the sales process. For NBI, expanding its portfolio beyond its traditional areas of operation in northern Bucharest represents a strategic growth priority, supported by the expansion of its consultant network and the continued strengthening of its developer partnerships.

data.title: Romania reportedly ready to cover part of the costs of maintaining US troops on its territory
data.description: Bucharest has joined other Eastern European governments, including Poland and the Baltic states, in proposing financial incentives for American military personnel, amid rising tensions in the Black Sea region, the sources told Bloomberg on condition of anonymity. Romania, which hosts around 1,000 US troops, was the first European country to experience troop reductions imposed by the Trump administration last year. The Pentagon is expected to complete a review of its military presence in Europe by the end of the year, which could lead to further cuts, Bloomberg reported. The Romanian government now plans to invest around EUR 4 billion by 2040 in the Mihail Kogălniceanu air base on the Black Sea coast, with the aim of accommodating more American or other foreign troops and providing them with better conditions, among other incentives, the sources said. Romanian authorities plan to increase defence spending to 5% of GDP, in line with NATO targets, from around 2.5% currently. Romania is also the second-largest recipient, after Poland, of funding under the EU’s common defence procurement programme, SAFE.

data.title: Romanian Liberals decide to give ‘necessity’ vote to team of PM-designate Luca Niculescu
data.description: The vote in the PNL’s leading body was decisive: only six of the 56 members voted against the proposal, while one abstained, Hotnews.ro reported. However, the decision followed lengthy debates, with some Liberal MPs questioning the choice to support a government formed mainly by members of the party that ousted Liberal PM Ilie Bolojan, in collaboration with the far-right Alliance for the Union of Romanians (AUR), on May 5 and continued its parliamentary cooperation with AUR. "Normally, the Liberal Party (PNL) would not have backed Niculescu’s PSD-dominated government, but Romania needs a functioning government to avoid the collapse of basic public institutions and services," Liberal leader and acting prime minister Ilie Bolojan explained. He stressed that the Liberals would remain in opposition. "We decided to position the party in opposition and grant a conditional and punctual ‘vote of necessity’ for the inauguration of the prime minister designated by the President of Romania," Bolojan announced after the party leadership meeting. Acting deputy prime minister Oana Gheorghiu and MEP Siegfried Mureșan also issued public statements explaining the PNL’s decision to vote for the cabinet proposed by Luca Niculescu. So far, PSD, PNL, the Hungarian party UDMR, the national minorities’ parliamentary group and the ‘United for Romania’ group of former prime minister Victor Ponta have expressed their support. If these parties and groups vote for the government at the joint session of the two parliamentary chambers on October 20, they will provide 279 votes, exceeding the 233 required for investiture. Luca Niculescu is the fourth prime minister-designate put forward by president Nicușor Dan since the government was ousted by a PSD-AUR no-confidence motion on May 5. The first nominee, presidential adviser Eugen Tomac, was replaced before reaching a parliamentary vote. His replacement, Adrian Vestea (PNL), marked an escalation in tensions between president Dan and PM Ilie Bolojan: Vestea was nominated without the Liberals’ consent, apparently with the aim of splitting the Liberal Party to the Social Democrats’ advantage. The third nominee, Liberal Siegfried Mureșan, was presented by president Dan as highly unlikely to secure a majority. Rather, the nomination appeared intended to give the president the option of dissolving Parliament after two failed investiture votes. By using his powers in this way for the first time, president Dan has created a solid parliamentary platform for independent PM-designate Luca Niculescu, who will serve as an interface for the PSD-led minority cabinet.

data.title: Romania’s use of gross energy resources shrinks by 6.3% y/y in January-August
data.description: While crude oil intake dropped by 21.1% y/y to 6.0 million toe and coal use fell by 17.3% y/y to just 1.1 million toe, imports of petroleum products surged by nearly 20% y/y to 2.7 million toe. Natural gas use increased by 2.7% y/y to 7.1 million toe, while imports rose by 10.8% y/y to 2.15 million toe as domestic production declined slightly, by 0.4% y/y, to 4.95 million toe. On the electricity market, production increased by 3.1% y/y to 33.3 TWh, driven by a 48% y/y surge in solar power generation to 5.17 TWh and a 13.5% y/y rise in hydropower generation to 9.17 TWh. Final consumption, in contrast, dropped by 4.0% y/y, improving the country’s external balance. Exports rose by 12.4% y/y to 10.5 TWh, while imports contracted by 6.3% y/y to 11.8 TWh. The trade balance remained negative, and the terms of trade are unfavourable, as most exports are carried out during peak hours, when electricity prices are typically higher than during off-peak hours.

data.title: Romania’s industrial output shows minor improvement in August, but maintains downward trend
data.description: The bigger picture, however, does not point to a sustainable or even relevant industrial recovery, contrasting the improvement in the PMI readings in Q3. In the first two months of the third quarter (Q3) taken together, the industrial output contracted by 3.6% y/y (-4.5% y/y for the core manufacturing industries) and in seasonally-adjusted terms edged down by 1.8% compared to the average level of Q2 (-2.6% for the manufacturing industries). The 12-month rolling industrial output contracted by 2.1% y/y as of August (-2.9% y/y for the manufacturing), visibly deteriorating from the -0.9% y/y (-1.2% y/y for manufacturing) annual decline in 2025 or -1.6% y/y (-1.1% y/y for manufacturing) in 2024. The value added generated by industry also contracted in the first two quarters of 2026, by 1.2% y/y and 3.9% y/y respectively. However, the decline is smoother than the sudden correction during 2023-2024, when the value added generated by industry plunged by some 27.5% from Q4 2022 to Q4 2024. Over the same two years, the gross industrial output edged down by only 1.4%. The value added deteriorated at a much faster pace because of rising energy prices eroding industrial margins. A similar effect is evident in Q2 compared with Q1 and could intensify in the coming quarters if energy prices stabilise at current high levels, driven by the war in the Middle East. BCR Romania Manufacturing PMI moved to expansionary territory for the first time since Q2 2024 and only the second time in the index's history. Romania’s PMI has remained in the expansionary territory for the second consecutive month in September, at 50.9 points, just below the 51.1 reading in August, prompting positive sentiment from analysts of Erste Group – which compiles the indicator. New orders and output sub-indicators remained the main drivers for expansion in September. PMI data pointed to a stronger second half of the year for manufacturing, which should provide broader support to the industrial sector according to Erste Group. Looking at the average PMI for the third quarter, it stands at 50.7, signaling a modest expansion in manufacturing activity. This marks the first quarter in expansion territory since Q2 2024 and only the second such occurrence in the index's history. Even so, 2026 is still likely to mark the fourth consecutive year of contraction in industrial output, the Austrian financial group admits. The ongoing conflict in the Middle East is exerting significant pressure on energy markets, raising costs for energy-intensive industries. Erste analysts believe a resolution of the war would provide some relief and be highly beneficial for domestic manufacturing. While substantial investments in EU security, along with large-scale fiscal stimulus in Germany targeting infrastructure and defense, are expected to support European industrial output, the recovery is likely to be uneven.

data.title: EC to assess Romania’s final EUR 6.4 bln in RRF funding by November 20
data.description: Romania has so far received EUR 13.27 billion under the RRF: EUR 8.95 billion in grants and EUR 4.32 billion in loans. The sum includes the EUR 301 million received on October 9 for targets and milestones under the third disbursement request, which was cleared with a delay. Of the EUR 1.65 billion in grants requested under the fifth payment request, around EUR 1.4 billion has already been cleared, interim investment and European projects minister Dragoș Pîslaru said, as reported by Economica.net . However, around EUR 900 million of the EUR 2.58 billion in grants requested under the sixth payment request is at risk due to unmet milestones, including the wage law for the public sector and missed decarbonisation targets. "This means that, from the two payment requests, we are looking at EUR 4.23 billion that we would still need to collect to raise the PNRR completion rate from the current 66% absorption rate for grants to over 90%, as we estimated," minister Pîslaru said. This remains feasible, he added, but depends heavily on the response from ministries, agencies and other authorities, which need to provide the required documents to the Commission. "To understand the timetable for payment request 6, it is very important to note that, around November 6, the Commission wants to conclude its assessment of payment request 6 and meet the deadline set by the regulation. In short, in the legislative area, this would mean that the Commission could make its final decision on November 20, allowing payment to be made in December," Pîslaru explained.

data.title: Romanian FinMin pledges credible 2027 budget ahead of parliamentary vote on new government
data.description: Nazare emphasised that efforts to reduce the budget deficit must continue in 2027, in an even more difficult context than this year, with significantly greater pressures and outstanding obligations. Nazare said that "the 2027 budget will be a major test of accountability" and that it must be built on realistic revenues, clear priorities and expenditure that the state can effectively support. "We cannot afford to repeat the mistake of turning unrealistic expectations into permanent budgetary obligations without the necessary resources to finance them. Any new objective must be accompanied by a simple question: where is the source of financing?" he said, as reported by Economedia.ro . The downside risk remains relevant. The finance minister argued that Romania has not yet reached the stage of relaunching growth without constraints, but remains in a phase of stabilisation and correcting past slippages. This is because the fragile balance in the eyes of investors is still being maintained with considerable effort. "Therefore, another essential objective today is to protect the sovereign rating and keep Romania out of the 'junk' category," he emphasised. Nazare recalled that Fitch's first rating assessment is scheduled for January, but warned that, in the event of a significant slippage, any other agency could immediately put Romania's rating under review by convening an ad hoc rating committee.

"We cannot afford to repeat the mistake of turning unrealistic expectations into permanent budgetary obligations without the necessary resources to finance them. Any new objective must be accompanied by a simple question: where is the source of financing?" he said, as reported by Economedia.ro . The downside risk remains relevant. The finance minister argued that Romania has not yet reached the stage of relaunching growth without constraints, but remains in a phase of stabilisation and correcting past slippages. This is because the fragile balance in the eyes of investors is still being maintained with considerable effort. "Therefore, another essential objective today is to protect the sovereign rating and keep Romania out of the 'junk' category," he emphasised. Nazare recalled that Fitch's first rating assessment is scheduled for January, but warned that, in the event of a significant slippage, any other agency could immediately put Romania's rating under review by convening an ad hoc rating committee.

data.title: Romania’s public deficit widens slightly in Q3, but remains moderate in January-September
data.description: Preliminary data discussed at a government meeting on October 16 indicated a slight deterioration in budget execution in Q3, but this does not put the full-year deficit target of 6.2% of GDP at risk, Economica.net reported. This is 1.45 percentage points (pp) below the 7.65% recorded in 2025. Revenues increased by 11.8% y/y to RON 523 billion, rising from 24.2% to 25.4% of GDP. Revenues from the national budget increased by 9.3% y/y, from 22.4% to 23.0% of GDP, marking a small real increase. Expenditures rose by only 5.5% y/y, while the expenditure-to-GDP ratio eased from 29.5% to 29.2%. Investment and interest expenditure rose sharply, while the rest of expenditure actually declined in nominal terms. Looking forward , the government can afford a deficit of 2.4% of GDP in Q4, slightly above the 2.3% recorded in the same period of 2025. Strong utilisation of transfers from the EU budget, particularly evident in Q3 and likely to continue in Q4, makes this target attainable. However, fiscal consolidation is losing one of its main drivers: the VAT rate base effects, which had contributed substantially to improving budget execution over the past year, had already dissipated by August. The new government, expected to take office on October 20, has to revise the 2026 budget while remaining within the fiscal targets. Drafting the 2027 budget plan may be an even more challenging task. Amid sluggish economic growth next year, a further 1 pp of consolidation, bringing the deficit to 5.2% of GDP in 2027, is becoming increasingly demanding for the new government, which has promised to present next year’s budget plan by the end of December. In 2026, the higher VAT rate, the freezing of wages and pensions, and the surge in EU transfers under RRF/PNRR accounted for most of the fiscal consolidation - but none of these drivers will remain in place next year. Regarding Q3 2026 budget execution , the deficit increased both in nominal terms (+15% y/y) and as a share of GDP, from 1.7% to 1.8%. However, for January-September as a whole, the deficit maintained its 23% y/y nominal contraction, while the deficit-to-GDP ratio decreased by 1.5 pp to 3.8%, from 5.3% in the same period of 2025 - slightly more than the 1.45 pp consolidation planned for the full year. Budget revenues increased by 14.8% y/y in Q3, according to calculations based on the preliminary budget execution data. Revenues from national sources increased by 9.9% y/y, mainly driven by a 24.4% increase in net VAT collection, although revenues from property taxes rose faster (+28.9% y/y). The latter, however, account for a relatively small share of total revenues. Notably, transfers from the EU budget soared by 86% y/y and accounted for 10.3% of total budget revenues in Q3, up from 6.4% in the same period of 2025. Public expenditure increased by 14.8% y/y in Q3, driven by a 44.5% y/y rise in interest payments on public debt and a 49% y/y increase in investment expenditure, which raised its share of total expenditure from 17% to 22%. The remaining expenditure, excluding investment and interest, increased by only 4.0% y/y in the quarter. This was mainly due to a 2.9% y/y decline in the public-sector wage bill and a marginal 1% y/y increase in social expenditure. In H1, expenditure excluding investment and interest had actually contracted by 3.6% y/y. Overall, this category of expenditure, which reflects the cost of running the public administration, contracted by 1.0% y/y in nominal terms. Further compression will require genuine reforms within the public administration.

data.title: Romanian F-16s shoot down two Geran drones over Black Sea
data.description: Two Romanian F-16 fighter jets shot down two Geran-family attack drones over the country’s territorial waters on Saturday, October 17, the Defense Ministry announced . Both drones were destroyed shortly after entering Romanian airspace. Military radar initially detected a group of aerial targets flying southwest approximately 120 kilometers east of Snake Island. Two F-16s on air-policing duty took off from the 86th Air Base at Borcea at 5:43 p.m. The first drone was shot down southeast of Sulina at 6:01 p.m., after spending two minutes in Romanian airspace, the ministry said. The second was destroyed east of Sulina at 6:05 p.m., following a five-minute incursion. The Defense Ministry identified them as jet-powered attack drones from the Geran family. https://www.facebook.com/mapn.ro/posts/pfbid0tmVhu4oU9eor8W1JUontuVnb9efXhGkyCB5zaSczdf11mEqTHxb4gSVrsWxwxCAal Interim defense minister Radu Miruță said the operation marked three firsts for the Romanian military, beginning with the rapid destruction of two consecutive targets by the same pair of fighter jets. “Two drones out of two that entered consecutively were shot down by the same crew, four and a half minutes apart. That is a first,” he stated, as quoted by News.ro . The minister also pointed to how quickly the first drone was intercepted, two minutes after crossing into Romanian airspace. He said statistical modeling had allowed the F-16s to position themselves in advance near the expected point of entry. “The fighter jets were waiting exactly at the point where the violation of Romanian airspace was estimated to occur, which demonstrates the very careful work carried out so far,” Radu Miruță said. The third first concerned the type of drone encountered. Minister Miruță explained that the targets were believed to be Russian Geran-4 drones capable of flying at approximately 450 kilometers per hour, considerably faster than the drones Romanian pilots had previously faced. “It is the first time we have shot down drones of this type,” he said. Before Saturday’s incident, Romanian military radar had detected aerial targets near the border in Ukrainian airspace on eight separate occasions during the previous week. Drones briefly entered Romanian airspace in four of those cases, according to the ministry. Six drones have been shot down over Romania since the beginning of 2026, while another 44 drones or fragments have been identified, recovered, or neutralized on Romanian territory, official Defense Ministry data showed. The ministry also said s everal commercial vessels had been struck by drones in the Black Sea during the previous week, including within Romanian territorial waters. It mentioned that response procedures were being continuously adjusted to protect national airspace and territorial waters.

data.title: Exim Banca Romaneasca Launches Private Banking Services
data.description: Exim Banca Romaneasca has launched its Private Banking Department, which provides personalized banking services, dedicated advisory support, and tailored wealth management solutions designed around the unique financial and investment goals of high-net-worth clients. Through its Private Banking services, Exim Banca Romaneasca offers a bespoke banking experience built around dedicated advisory support, close relationship management, and a comprehensive approach to addressing clients' financial needs. The offering is available to clients holding assets worth more than RON 1 million managed through the bank. "In Private Banking, true value is defined not only by the financial solutions we offer, but by the relationships we build with each client. This offering is the result of the trust our clients have placed in us over the years and of our deep understanding of their financial goals. Exim Banca Romaneasca's expertise allows us to meet these expectations through personalized services and solutions tailored to each client's specific needs." said Traian Halalai, Executive President of Exim Banca Romaneasca. The current offering includes a comprehensive range of savings and financing solutions designed around each client's objectives, including customized deposits with flexible maturities and preferential interest rates, foreign exchange services under advantageous conditions, savings accounts, and lending products with competitive terms. In the near future, the bank will further expand the investment component of its Private Banking services through tailored products and advisory solutions aligned with clients' investment profiles and financial aspirations, supporting efficient wealth diversification and long-term added value. Private Banking services are currently available in Bucharest. In response to the increasing demand for personalized wealth management services, the bank plans to extend this model into Romania's main economic cities, providing a broader client base with access to specialized financial expertise, investment opportunities, and premium banking services. Exim Banca Romaneasca is a 100% Romanian-owned universal bank and ranks among the top 10 largest credit institutions in Romania by assets. The bank recently received its first rating from the international agency Fitch Ratings, reaffirming Exim Banca Romaneasca's financial strength and stability.

data.title: Auchan Romania introduces new in-store digital concept in Bucharest hypermarket
data.description: Auchan Romania has introduced its new in-store digital concept, Auchan Retail Media, at the Auchan Drumul Taberei hypermarket in Bucharest. The concept features two immersive LED entrances and 12 digital formats integrated into the store’s architecture. Each entrance has a curved LED screen measuring 3.5 × 5.3 meters, covering more than 18 sqm above shoppers’ heads. Approximately 650,000 monthly visitors pass beneath these screens at the store. At the 10,500 sqm store, the average duration of a visit is 45 minutes and 70% of customers visit once a week or more, the company said. The store is fitted with 24 LED screens, 50 central screens and 7 screens in special formats, offering brands 12 communication formats. These include double-sided digital pillars with 3D effects in the Fresh area and food court, a 25-metre LED header in the BeautyShop area, and screens integrated into the Wine Cellar, Beverages, Home & Seasonal, Textiles, Baby Care and Trend sections. The company worked with Romanian startup Spectro:o to implement the solution. The startup was founded in Sibiu by entrepreneur Marius Pătroi. Auchan invested EUR 200,000 to implement the new concept in its Drumul Taberei store, part of approximately EUR 3 million put into the development of its retail media ecosystem. In the coming period, Auchan plans to implement the concept at its Floreasca and Sun Plaza stores, also in Bucharest, adapted to the areas of the two units. Later, the concept will be implemented in other malls. “Customers no longer simply walk past a screen; they step into an experience. With immersive LED entrances, the store’s architecture itself becomes a communication medium, while the experience continues through digital formats integrated into every shopping zone. This allows brands to reach customers at the exact moment purchase decisions are made, with results that can be directly measured through sales. This marks a new chapter for retail media in Romania, and we invite you to discover it at our Auchan Drumul Taberei store,” Tiberiu Dănețiu, Executive Board Member and Director of Retail Media & Institutional Affairs at Auchan Romania, explained. Tiberiu Dănețiu    Photo: Auchan An eye-tracking study conducted in 2025 in Auchan stores by academics from the Faculty of Marketing at the Bucharest University of Economic Studies (ASE) showed “all participating shoppers noticed the screens, which remained within their field of vision for up to 25% of the time they spent shopping.” A separate exit survey presented by the company found that over 60% of shoppers accurately recalled the advertisements they had seen, while 30% of shoppers who had not purchased the advertised product intended to buy it on their next visit. In terms of effectiveness, measurements showed that for well-established brands, sales conversion rates can reach 15–20% or even higher, driven solely by in-store screen advertising, without any additional promotional activations, the company said. The retail media network Auchan Retail Media is a data-driven, omnichannel 360° communication ecosystem that integrates physical and digital media solutions in-store, as well as on-site and off-site digital advertising. Auchan launched coordinated retail media initiatives in 2017, when it equipped its first store with connected digital screens. This was followed in 2021 by the launch of the country’s first retail media sales house. Today, the Auchan Retail Media & Data Insights ecosystem brings together approximately 1,000 digital screens across 100 stores, connected through Auchan Instore TV, alongside online, CRM and off-site advertising solutions. More than 300 companies across FMCG, food, non-food and non-retail sectors use the ecosystem, with brands having run approximately 6,000 advertising campaigns to date. At its core is a first-party data foundation as over 60% of daily sales across Auchan stores are made using the retailer's loyalty card. In the next phase, Auchan Retail Media plans to expand its digital advertising capabilities, AI-powered solutions and programmatic advertising, with a strong focus on personalization. Auchan Romania, which opened its first hypermarket in the country twenty years ago, operates a network of more than 500 stores, including 26 traditional hypermarkets, nine ATAC Hiper Discount hypermarkets and one ATAC Super Discount store, nine traditional supermarkets, the Auchan Go smart store, nearly 400 MyAuchan convenience stores, most of which are located at Petrom service stations, and more than 70 Simply by Auchan franchise stores, alongside its online store. The company also offers a range of solutions for partners and customers, in addition to its energy supply company, Auchan Renewable Energy. Auchan had a turnover including taxes of more than EUR 1.7 billion in 2024.

data.title: BT Capital Partners trading accounts opened through BT Pay double since June to 35,000
data.description: BT Capital Partners, the investment banking and capital markets division of Banca Transilvania Group, said it reached 35,000 stock trading accounts opened through the BT Pay app, double the number recorded in June 2026. The growth was driven by the integration of investment services into BT Pay, as well as by the launch of a new product from the Banca Transilvania Group, the BT Romania ETF, which is trading on the Bucharest Stock Exchange. The new investors are primarily clients of Banca Transilvania’s Private and Premium Banking segments, with most accounts opened by clients in Cluj-Napoca, Bucharest, Constanța, Iași, and Timișoara. “The rapid increase in the number of accounts opened through BT Pay shows us that investing is becoming more accessible to an increasingly large number of people. We are seeing a shift in mindset, with people complementing saving with an interest in building long-term wealth,” Daniela Secară, CEO of BT Capital Partners, explained. More than 90,000 people invest on the Bucharest Stock Exchange through BT Capital Partners. The expansion of its client base has helped the company’s net assets exceed RON 40 billion (approximately EUR 8 billion), the company said.

data.title: Russian Attack Cuts Power, Water Across Ukraine’s West
data.description: Russian forces launched missiles and 269 drones at Ukraine overnight into Monday, Oct. 19, damaging civilian and energy infrastructure across several western regions. Two women were wounded in the Rivne region, with Volyn reporting about 66,000 metering points without power, while parts of the Vinnytsia region and the central city lost electricity and water. In Zubra, Lviv region, debris damaged 11 homes, a garage, and eight cars, with no injuries reported.

data.title: Language Lab Marks 10 Years With Launch of Ukraine Connected

data.title: France Reeling From Cost-of-Living Riots as 1,800 Arrested
data.description: France was assessing extensive damage following violent nationwide protests on Oct. 17 over the cost of living, which saw 1,800 people arrested and 500 security personnel injured. Demonstrations drawing between 550,000 and 800,000 participants turned destructive on the margins, resulting in the arson of Limoges’ 19th-century town hall, widespread looting of 1,500 businesses with damages in the hundreds of millions of euros, and a severed hand sustained by a 17-year-old from a tear gas grenade. The crisis prompted French President Emmanuel Macron to schedule an address to the nation as Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu convened a crisis cabinet session amid heated political disputes between Marine Le Pen and Jean-Luc Mélenchon ahead of upcoming elections.

data.title: Russian ‘Matryoshka’ Bot Farm Targets US Midterms With AI
data.description: A Bloomberg News investigation revealed that the Russian state-backed disinformation operation “Matryoshka” is deploying automated bot farms to inflate view counts of AI-generated videos attacking Democratic candidates ahead of the US midterms. The campaign produced synthetic videos mimicking prominent actors and fabricated news broadcasts from ABC and CBS targeting candidates in 20 Senate and 29 gubernatorial races. Forensic data from Antibot4Navalny showed view numbers spiking to 200,000 within an hour before flatlining, driven by dormant bot profiles. The disclosures follow ODNI warnings on AI election interference and coincide with network disruptions following Ukrainian drone strikes on Yandex data centers.

data.title: Sybiha: 76 Energy Strikes Prove Moscow Flouts Ceasefire
data.description: Ukraine’s Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha has declared that 76 Russian strikes against Ukraine’s energy sector over the past week prove Moscow has honored no commitments since US President Donald Trump declared an “energy ceasefire.” Highlighting a weekly barrage of nearly 2,700 drones, 1,700 guided bombs, and 66 missiles, Sybiha warned that the Kremlin is imitating diplomacy to secure economic accommodations. He cautioned Western partners that waiving sanctions or easing economic pressure merely injects fresh hard currency into the Russian military budget, urging allies to intensify economic deterrence and bolster Ukrainian air defenses ahead of winter.

data.title: RAF Jets Log Near Misses With Suspected Drones at High Altitude
data.description: British Royal Air Force flight logs have revealed near misses with unidentified aerial objects on at least two occasions during training exercises. An RAF Voyager tanker refueling a Typhoon over Norfolk encountered a potential drone at 17,000 feet – over 40 times the UK commercial limit of 400 feet – forcing the pilot to instinctively duck. Days later, a Typhoon pilot engaged in combat maneuvers 30 miles off the English coast spotted a circular black object at 12,500 feet.

data.title: Trump Envoys Push Russian Gas Transit in Ukraine Peace Talks
data.description: US special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner have proposed restoring Russian natural gas transit through Ukraine as an economic incentive in prospective peace negotiations. The White House argues transit revenue would aid Kyiv while enticing Moscow to end the war, with discussions even touching upon Nord Stream 2. The concept drew opposition from European allies, especially Germany, where Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s security adviser Günter Sautter and former Economy Minister Robert Habeck firmly rejected renewing dependencies on Russian hydrocarbons despite domestic political pressure from the AfD.

data.title: Thwarted Arson at Lithuanian Starlink Site Triggers Security Review
data.description: Lithuanian Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevičius announced that security services thwarted an overnight arson attempt targeting a domestic company storing Starlink satellite communications equipment, having warned the enterprise and reinforced security in advance. The incident coincided with an unidentified drone breaching Lithuanian airspace on Sunday morning, prompting Sinkevičius to convene an emergency meeting of the National Security Commission on Oct. 19 to examine debris, trace flight paths, and consider expanded statutory powers for neutralizing unmanned aircraft amid heightened Baltic vigilance against Russian hybrid sabotage.

data.title: Russian Strike Hits Odesa High-Rise, Injures 2
data.description: A Russian strike has hit a multi-story residential building in a densely populated neighborhood of Odesa and damaged regional power installations, injuring two civilians – including a 13-year-old girl – and leaving 24,100 households without power. Regional authorities confirmed a roof blaze and damage to top-floor apartments, prompting the establishment of on-site operational headquarters. Ukrainian energy operator DTEK reported extensive damage requiring prolonged repairs, triggering emergency blackouts across Bilhorod-Dnistrovskyi, Izmail, and Bolhrad districts.

data.title: Russia’s Rassvet Network Threatens Ukraine With Real-Time Strike Control
data.description: Presidential defense technology adviser Serhii Beskrestnov warned that Russia’s emerging “Rassvet” low-orbit satellite constellation could provide continuous real-time guidance for Shahed strike drones, reconnaissance UAVs, and Banderol and Dan-M cruise missiles across Ukraine within six months. Developed by Bureau 1440, the system threatens to bypass Ukrainian electronic warfare defenses by enabling dynamic mid-flight adjustments. Beskrestnov described the constellation as Moscow’s foremost technological threat, while Ukrainian authorities accelerate countermeasure developments and lobby international regulators to block Rassvet’s operational footprint.

data.title: DSP o Maquiavélico Ganancioso
data.description: Guineenses, mais uma vez, venho para vos alertar sobre o perigo que Domingos Simões Pereira representa para a Guiné-Bissau. Faço esse alerta a todos os guineenses sem exceção que se encontre no país ou no estrangeiro, ao PAIGC em especial e na pessoa do Cipriano Cassamá em concreto. Alerta esse sobre o verdadeiro DSP, o verdadeiro espírito que move esse sujeito, o qual alguns ainda continuam a acreditar para não dizer adorar. Domingos Simões Pereira é um manipulador, um verdadeiro chantagista e calculista provavelmente, tipo de comportamento que ultrapassa o nível de psicopata. U m ambicioso desmedido, um verdadeiro criminoso que sabe como e quando cometer o crime. Ele jamais coabitaria não só com JOMAV, assim como com qualquer presidente que seria eleito, a não ser o que ele apoiou disfarçadamente. Isto porque ele tem sua própria agenda, e o PAIGC é simplesmente uma plataforma para sua concretização. DSP jamais coabitaria com JOMAV porque o seu candidato preferido era o Paulo Gomes e sempre será, o qual juntamente com Tchitchi vão delineando mecanismo de modo a serem os novos donos da Guiné-Bissau. Segundo eles este é um processo a médio prazo, e é preciso coragem e paciência para concretiza-lo. Ganhar o congresso não importa em que circunstância e ter novamente o partido na mão, é uma fase concluída em proveito deles, enquanto verdadeiros militantes do PAIGC estão a bater palmas. Depois dessa eleição legislativa, não importa o resultado, o Cipriano Cassama que se prepare a mala ou fica de bico fechado, pois o candidato preferido para o partido será o Paulo Gomes, e esse sim deve ter a voz dentro do partido. DSP é um ambicioso desmedido, nunca teve consideração por ninguém, JOMAV muito menos, o sujeito é um maquiavélico nato, Cipriano Casama será descartado quando menos esperar podes tomar a nota. Guineenses, falar do Paulo Gomes e Tchitchi é falar do MCCI e demais outras organizações e personalidades camufladas no nosso país. Esses dois indivíduos são os principais financiadores do MCCI e demais outras personalidades boca de aluguel na cidade de Bissau. O MCCI, Milícia idealizado por JBV e DSP, agora financiado e dirigido por "futuro triângulo do poder" ou seja, "DSP, Paulo Gomes e Tchitchi", têm 3 principais objectivos: 1º Perturbar a ordem pública em nome da cidadania, difamar e tentar descredibilizar qualquer que seja organizações ou indivíduos não alinhados ao triângulo, de modo a suportar suas caminhadas na busca do poder. 2º Caso se concretize o objectivo do triângulo, o papel da Milícia do MCCI passará a ser de vigilância constante a todos os adversários de modo a garantir falsa paz social e o poder de controlo. 3º Tentar ganhar credibilidade junto das organizações internacionais e regionais, através de suas visitas e actividades de fachada, para quando houver as tais actividades de perturbações de ordem pública, poderem ganhar notoriedade. Mas isso não deve preocupar ninguém, pois estão bem identificados e bem caçados, dentro e fora da Guiné-Bissau. Não tenho nada contra ninguém, mas quem continuar a perturbar verdadeira paz social dos guineenses em troca de benefícios como sempre foi nos últimos anos dessa crise, e que sempre tenho tolerado, então que fique claro "estou firme e determinado para tudo e todos". Para finalizar, gostaria de vos deixar uma reflexão com a seguinte frase: " Domingos Simões Pereira é um perigo grave para o futuro do país ". Isto porque publicar aqui tudo que é necessário para provar ou sustentar a razão dessa frase, só pode agravar ainda mais a paz social que tanto necessitamos. Chega, chega não podemos continuar a viver nessa turbulência vida toda, meus irmãos guineenses, não é saudável, é tóxico, não é justo para um povo que tanto sofreu. U m ambicioso desmedido, um verdadeiro criminoso que sabe como e quando cometer o crime. Ele jamais coabitaria não só com JOMAV, assim como com qualquer presidente que seria eleito, a não ser o que ele apoiou disfarçadamente. Isto porque ele tem sua própria agenda, e o PAIGC é simplesmente uma plataforma para sua concretização. DSP jamais coabitaria com JOMAV porque o seu candidato preferido era o Paulo Gomes e sempre será, o qual juntamente com Tchitchi vão delineando mecanismo de modo a serem os novos donos da Guiné-Bissau. Depois dessa eleição legislativa, não importa o resultado, o Cipriano Cassama que se prepare a mala ou fica de bico fechado, pois o candidato preferido para o partido será o Paulo Gomes, e esse sim deve ter a voz dentro do partido. DSP é um ambicioso desmedido, nunca teve consideração por ninguém, JOMAV muito menos, o sujeito é um maquiavélico nato, Cipriano Casama será descartado quando menos esperar podes tomar a nota. Guineenses, falar do Paulo Gomes e Tchitchi é falar do MCCI e demais outras organizações e personalidades camufladas no nosso país. Esses dois indivíduos são os principais financiadores do MCCI e demais outras personalidades boca de aluguel na cidade de Bissau. O MCCI, Milícia idealizado por JBV e DSP, agora financiado e dirigido por "futuro triângulo do poder" ou seja, "DSP, Paulo Gomes e Tchitchi", têm 3 principais objectivos: 1º Perturbar a ordem pública em nome da cidadania, difamar e tentar descredibilizar qualquer que seja organizações ou indivíduos não alinhados ao triângulo, de modo a suportar suas caminhadas na busca do poder. 2º Caso se concretize o objectivo do triângulo, o papel da Milícia do MCCI passará a ser de vigilância constante a todos os adversários de modo a garantir falsa paz social e o poder de controlo. 3º Tentar ganhar credibilidade junto das organizações internacionais e regionais, através de suas visitas e actividades de fachada, para quando houver as tais actividades de perturbações de ordem pública, poderem ganhar notoriedade. Mas isso não deve preocupar ninguém, pois estão bem identificados e bem caçados, dentro e fora da Guiné-Bissau. Não tenho nada contra ninguém, mas quem continuar a perturbar verdadeira paz social dos guineenses em troca de benefícios como sempre foi nos últimos anos dessa crise, e que sempre tenho tolerado, então que fique claro "estou firme e determinado para tudo e todos". data.title: DSP, UM PERIGO GRAVE PARA FUTURO DO PAÍS
data.description: Os meios de comunicação também são as formas de manipulação mais utilizadas pelos poderes políticos, dado o seu impacto social. As informações são manipuladas não apenas tendo em vista omitir factos relevantes, mas também distorcer o conteúdo da informação veiculada, produzir ou forjar a opinião pública, de modo que a mesma se ajuste às ideias dos gananciosos. A única forma dos cidadãos evitarem cair nestes processos de manipulação é tornarem-se mais vigilantes em relação às instituições democráticas e aos órgãos de informação, adoptando uma atitude de permanente reflexão crítica sobre a informação que lhes é fornecida. Na Guiné-Bissau, nos últimos anos, cresceu exponencialmente o número de pessoas mediocres, pessoas sem escrúpulos ligadas à produção de rádios e outros meios de comunicação com influencia na nossa sociedade, gente que apesar da sua enorme influência na sociedade, trabalha na mais completa impunidade e sem qualquer controlo ético/democrático. Obcecado pelo poder, ciente da dificuldade do povo guineense em avaliar informações, ciente do poder dos instrumentos de comunicação, Domingos Simões Pereira (DSP) nunca menosprezou esses instrumentos para atingir seu objectivo, sempre usou-os de forma desonesta como agora está a fazer tudo por tudo para manter no controlo desses veicúlos, mesmo que isso custe a vida dos outros. Governou na corrupção, no nepotismo e no desvios de somas astronómicas do dinheiro de povo, que muito serviria para investimentos na saúde, educação e outros serviços publicos, para beneficiar familiares e amigos. Finge que preocupa com os problemas do país, mas só engana o povo honesto, humilde e trabalhador que infelizmente sofre muito, não sei até quando, devido a sua paciência e tolerância aos governantes como DSP, criminoso travestido em politico que vive na custa de povo e acima de tudo ainda fa-lo refem do próprio suor. Roubou e decepcionou tanto não só aos guineenses assim como a comunidade internacional que sempre acreditou que o sujeito era ideal para ajudar esse povo a sair do ciclo de sofrimento que parece infinito. Foi demitido, não conformou e está a fazer tudo na medida do possível para continuar a complicar a vida dos guineenses. Razão disso é que depois de perder a batalha nos meios de comunicações mais modernos nomeadamente os blogues onde investiu grandes somas do dinheiro de povo, para fazer a lavagem cerebral dos menos instruídos e não só. Fugiu do facebook onde sempre frequentava e comunicava com todos tentado passar a mensagem de um politico moderno e aberto a diálogo/opiniões, mas que afinal era simplesmente um falso modernista. Caiu a mascara e já não consegue enganar ninguem, pois a sua credibilidade está abaixo de zero, para não dizer outra coisa. Camaradas, para conhecimento geral, com o dinheiro roubado que custou suor de povo guineense, DSP decidiu avançar com um outro novo plano maquiavelico, para criar a sua própria estação de rádio. As informações são manipuladas não apenas tendo em vista omitir factos relevantes, mas também distorcer o conteúdo da informação veiculada, produzir ou forjar a opinião pública, de modo que a mesma se ajuste às ideias dos gananciosos. A única forma dos cidadãos evitarem cair nestes processos de manipulação é tornarem-se mais vigilantes em relação às instituições democráticas e aos órgãos de informação, adoptando uma atitude de permanente reflexão crítica sobre a informação que lhes é fornecida. Na Guiné-Bissau, nos últimos anos, cresceu exponencialmente o número de pessoas mediocres, pessoas sem escrúpulos ligadas à produção de rádios e outros meios de comunicação com influencia na nossa sociedade, gente que apesar da sua enorme influência na sociedade, trabalha na mais completa impunidade e sem qualquer controlo ético/democrático. Obcecado pelo poder, ciente da dificuldade do povo guineense em avaliar informações, ciente do poder dos instrumentos de comunicação, Domingos Simões Pereira (DSP) nunca menosprezou esses instrumentos para atingir seu objectivo, sempre usou-os de forma desonesta como agora está a fazer tudo por tudo para manter no controlo desses veicúlos, mesmo que isso custe a vida dos outros. Governou na corrupção, no nepotismo e no desvios de somas astronómicas do dinheiro de povo, que muito serviria para investimentos na saúde, educação e outros serviços publicos, para beneficiar familiares e amigos. Finge que preocupa com os problemas do país, mas só engana o povo honesto, humilde e trabalhador que infelizmente sofre muito, não sei até quando, devido a sua paciência e tolerância aos governantes como DSP, criminoso travestido em politico que vive na custa de povo e acima de tudo ainda fa-lo refem do próprio suor. Roubou e decepcionou tanto não só aos guineenses assim como a comunidade internacional que sempre acreditou que o sujeito era ideal para ajudar esse povo a sair do ciclo de sofrimento que parece infinito. Foi demitido, não conformou e está a fazer tudo na medida do possível para continuar a complicar a vida dos guineenses. Razão disso é que depois de perder a batalha nos meios de comunicações mais modernos nomeadamente os blogues onde investiu grandes somas do dinheiro de povo, para fazer a lavagem cerebral dos menos instruídos e não só. Fugiu do facebook onde sempre frequentava e comunicava com todos tentado passar a mensagem de um politico moderno e aberto a diálogo/opiniões, mas que afinal era simplesmente um falso modernista. Caiu a mascara e já não consegue enganar ninguem, pois a sua credibilidade está abaixo de zero, para não dizer outra coisa. Camaradas, para conhecimento geral, com o dinheiro roubado que custou suor de povo guineense, DSP decidiu avançar com um outro novo plano maquiavelico, para criar a sua própria estação de rádio. data.title: DSP não respeita os antigos combatentes e sempre usou e abusou desses camaradas. Prova disso é que continuou a governar mesmo já com Carlos Correia como primeiro ministro. Usou até o cadáver de Carmem Perreira para promover sua imagem, pois é sabido que a malograda como sendo antigo combatente e membro do PAIGC o corpo só deveria passar por ANP e sede do partido e nunca na Primatura como aconteceu, e por cima de tudo com indivíduos alí barricados por vontade própria vandalizando instituição do estado o que demonstra uma clara promoção ao anarquismo. Não respeitou nem o Pai da Nação(ALC), nem o PR quanto mais o formalismo de um estado de direito democrático, prova disso mais uma vez, o ganancioso após o PR ter depositado coroas de flores no túmulo de ALC no dia dos heróis nacionais, reuniu os seus "gangs" para o mesmo efeito, conseguiu até mobilizar um dos familiares do Pai da Nação para lhe acompanhar tudo isso para manipular e dividir os guineenses "guineenses ku udjus fitchadu" para os seus intereses obscuros.

data.title: Na vijf jaar krijgen vissers in Coronie eindelijk weer visvergunningen
data.description: Vijf jaar lang moesten vissers in Coronie zonder geldige vergunning hun werk doen. Voor twaalf van hen komt daar nu verandering in. Volgens parlementariër Leroy Doorson worden vandaag de eerste vergunningen uitgereikt. Minister Mike Noersalim werkt aan de verlenging van de overige vergunningen, die mogelijk nog deze maand worden afgehandeld. The post Na vijf jaar krijgen vissers in Coronie eindelijk weer visvergunningen appeared first on Suriname Herald .

data.title: Braziliaan verkoopt alles voor zijn grote liefde, maar droomvrouw blijkt door AI gemaakt
data.description: Hij dacht de liefde van zijn leven te hebben gevonden, verkocht zijn bezittingen en reisde ongeveer 2000 kilometer om haar eindelijk in de armen te sluiten. Maar voor de 49-jarige Braziliaan Edimar Martins liep zijn liefdesavontuur uit op een pijnlijke ontgoocheling. Zijn droomvrouw bleek niet van vlees en bloed, maar een digitaal personage dat met kunstmatige intelligentie was gemaakt. Toch weigert de metselaar zijn zoektocht naar de ware liefde op te geven. The post Braziliaan verkoopt alles voor zijn grote liefde, maar droomvrouw blijkt door AI gemaakt appeared first on Suriname Herald .

data.title: Binnenland krijgt eerste landbouwopleiding: 90 studenten starten met pre-bachelor- en bachelortraject
